lessonPlans.title: Colors Everywhere
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Preschoolers will explore colors through hands-on play, movement, art, songs, books, sensory experiences, and everyday discoveries. Throughout the week, children will identify, sort, match, mix, create, and talk about colors while developing language, problem-solving, fine motor skills, and creativity.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Identify and explore a variety of colors in the environment
Build color vocabulary through play and conversation
Practice sorting, matching, and pattern skills with colors
Strengthen fine motor and gross motor development through color activities
Encourage creativity through open-ended art experiences
Promote social interaction and cooperative color play

lessonPlans.observationOpportunities: Observe color recognition, matching and pattern skills, language use, participation in activities, fine motor development, and social interactions during color play.
lessonPlans.adaptations: Provide larger materials for easier grasping. Offer hand-over-hand support when needed. Focus on exploration and exposure rather than requiring color mastery.
lessonPlans.familyConnection: Encourage families to point out colors during daily routines. Ask children to find colors at home, in the grocery store, outdoors, and during playtime.

items.title: Color Hunt Adventure
items.objective: Introduce and explore colors found in the classroom.
items.description: Preschoolers search for colorful objects around the room and place them into matching color baskets.
items.materials: Color baskets, classroom objects, color picture cards
items.setup: Place colored baskets around the room with a few sample objects in each.
items.steps:
1. Introduce color baskets and name each color.
2. Invite children to find objects that match each basket color.
3. Place objects into baskets and discuss discoveries together.
4. Count how many items are in each basket.
5. Celebrate successful color finds.
items.teacherRole: Guide children as they search, identify, and sort colors.
items.observationOpportunities:
Identifies colors
Matches objects to baskets
Participates in group activity
items.adaptations: Provide visual steps, partner support, or a simplified materials set. Extend with an open-ended challenge for children ready for more.

3. Talk about colors being used and new colors created.

items.title: Pom-Pom Color Sort
items.objective: Practice matching and sorting colors using fine motor skills.
items.description: Preschoolers sort pom-poms into matching colored cups or bowls.

items.setup: Arrange colored cups on a table with a bowl of mixed pom-poms.
items.steps:
1. Introduce the colored cups and name each color.
2. Demonstrate sorting one pom-pom into the matching cup.
3. Invite children to sort at their own pace.
4. Discuss colors and compare quantities in each cup.
5. Celebrate successful sorting.

items.title: Color Pattern Building

items.description: Preschoolers use blocks or beads to build repeating color patterns.

items.setup: Place blocks and sample pattern cards at a table.
items.steps:
1. Show a simple two-color pattern such as red-blue-red-blue.
2. Invite children to copy the pattern with blocks.
3. Encourage children to create their own patterns.
4. Name the colors in each pattern aloud together.
5. Display finished patterns for classmates to see.

items.title: Primary Color Mixing Lab
items.objective: Explore how primary colors combine to make new colors.
items.description: Preschoolers mix red, blue, and yellow paint or water to discover secondary colors.
items.materials: Red, blue, and yellow paint or colored water, clear cups, droppers, white paper
items.setup: Set up mixing trays with small amounts of each primary color.
items.steps:
1. Review the three primary colors.
2. Invite children to predict what happens when two colors mix.
3. Mix small amounts and observe the new colors.
4. Paint swatches of each discovery on paper.
5. Discuss favorite color combinations.
items.teacherRole: Ask prediction questions and narrate color changes during mixing.
items.observationOpportunities:

items.objective: Build color recognition through active searching.
items.description: Preschoolers carry color cards on a walk through the classroom or outdoor space to find matching items.
items.materials: Color cards, collection bags or baskets
items.setup: Give each child or pair a color card before the hunt begins.
items.steps:
1. Show the focus color card and name the color together.
2. Walk slowly and search for matching objects.

5. Draw pictures of items that cannot be moved.

items.title: Color Freeze Dance
items.objective: Practice listening skills while reinforcing color names.
items.description: Preschoolers dance when music plays and freeze while holding up a named color card.
items.materials: Music player, color cards, open space
items.setup: Place color cards where children can reach them during the game.
items.steps:
1. Explain that children dance when music plays and freeze when it stops.
2. When frozen, hold up the color card that is called.
3. Play several rounds with different colors.
4. Invite children to take turns calling a color.
5. End with a calm stretch and color name review.
items.teacherRole: Control music, call colors, and model freezing positions.

items.steps:

lessonPlans.title: All About Me
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Preschoolers will explore who they are through activities focused on their names, families, bodies, feelings, preferences, and unique characteristics. Through books, songs, art, mirrors, movement, and discussions, children will build self-awareness, confidence, communication skills, and positive relationships with others.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Develop self-awareness and confidence
Learn and recognize their names and letters in names
Explore body parts and facial features
Build emotional awareness and vocabulary
Strengthen communication skills
Celebrate similarities and differences among peers

items.title: Mirror Me

items.setup: Place mirrors at child eye level with emotion cards nearby.
items.steps:
1. Invite children to look into mirrors.
2. Point out eyes, nose, mouth, and ears.
3. Encourage children to identify features on themselves.
4. Make faces to match emotion cards.
5. Discuss what makes each face unique.

Uses vocabulary

lessonPlans.title: Dinosaur Discovery
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Children will travel back to prehistoric times as they investigate dinosaurs through hands-on exploration, dramatic play, sensory experiences, STEM challenges, art, movement, and early literacy activities. Throughout the week, children will become paleontologists, discover fossils, compare dinosaur sizes, explore volcanoes, and strengthen kindergarten readiness skills through engaging dinosaur-themed learning.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Develop curiosity about prehistoric animals
Strengthen observation and investigation skills
Build vocabulary related to dinosaurs and fossils
Practice counting, sorting, and measuring
Encourage imaginative dramatic play
Strengthen fine and gross motor development
Promote problem-solving and critical thinking
Foster cooperation through group activities

lessonPlans.title: Healthy Habits
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Children will learn how healthy choices help their bodies grow strong. Throughout the week, children will explore nutrition, exercise, hygiene, sleep, dental health, and self-care through hands-on activities, movement games, dramatic play, experiments, and creative experiences. Children will build lifelong healthy habits while strengthening social, physical, and cognitive skills.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Identify healthy foods and healthy habits
Learn the importance of exercise and movement
Understand proper handwashing techniques
Explore dental health and hygiene routines
Develop self-care skills and independence
Practice healthy decision-making
Strengthen fine and gross motor skills
Build vocabulary related to health and wellness

lessonPlans.observationOpportunities: Observe children's understanding of healthy choices, participation in self-care routines, ability to identify healthy foods, gross motor development during exercise activities, and communication during discussions.
lessonPlans.adaptations: Provide visual supports for routines. Offer adaptive tools when needed. Break activities into smaller steps and allow children multiple ways to participate.
lessonPlans.familyConnection: Encourage families to involve children in healthy daily routines. Talk about healthy foods, handwashing, exercise, and bedtime habits at home. Invite children to share healthy choices they make with their families.

lessonPlans.title: Around the World
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Children will travel around the world through imaginative play, cultural exploration, music, art, movement, and hands-on learning experiences. Throughout the week, children will discover different countries, traditions, foods, landmarks, languages, and celebrations while developing an appreciation for diversity and global communities.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Explore different cultures and traditions
Develop awareness of similarities and differences
Learn about world landmarks and geography
Build vocabulary related to travel and culture
Strengthen social-emotional skills through cultural appreciation
Practice counting, sorting, and comparing
Develop creativity through multicultural art experiences
Foster curiosity about the world

lessonPlans.title: Ocean Explorers
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Children will dive into an exciting underwater adventure as they explore ocean animals, habitats, waves, coral reefs, and ocean conservation. Through hands-on investigations, sensory experiences, dramatic play, art projects, and STEM challenges, children will discover the wonders of the ocean while developing curiosity, creativity, and critical thinking skills.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Identify common ocean animals and habitats
Develop scientific observation skills
Explore floating and sinking concepts
Strengthen vocabulary related to ocean life
Practice sorting, counting, and comparing
Develop fine and gross motor skills
Encourage imaginative play and storytelling
Foster appreciation for ocean conservation
lessonPlans.weeklyMaterials:
Toy ocean animals
Shells
Blue water beads
Sand
Water table
Fishing nets
Magnifying glasses
Paint
Markers
Construction paper
Glue
Blocks
Plastic containers
Measuring cups
Books
Music player
lessonPlans.vocabularyWords:
Ocean
Wave
Coral
Reef
Fish
Shark
Whale
Dolphin
Octopus
Jellyfish
Habitat
Shell
Float
Sink
lessonPlans.observationOpportunities: Observe children's curiosity during investigations, use of ocean vocabulary, ability to classify animals, participation in cooperative play, and understanding of ocean habitats.
lessonPlans.adaptations: Provide visual supports and picture cards. Offer adaptive tools when needed. Allow children multiple ways to participate through art, discussion, movement, and sensory exploration.
lessonPlans.familyConnection: Encourage families to talk about ocean animals and water habitats. Visit a library to explore ocean-themed books and discuss ways to help keep oceans clean.

lessonPlans.title: Seasons of the Year
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Children will explore the four seasons through hands-on investigations, sensory experiences, art, dramatic play, movement activities, and nature exploration. Throughout the week, children will discover how weather, plants, animals, clothing, and activities change throughout the year while building observation skills and scientific thinking.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Identify the four seasons
Observe seasonal changes in nature
Compare weather patterns
Develop vocabulary related to seasons and weather
Strengthen sorting and classification skills
Explore seasonal clothing and activities
Develop fine and gross motor skills
Foster curiosity about the natural world
lessonPlans.weeklyMaterials:
Season picture cards
Weather charts
Leaves
Artificial flowers
Cotton balls
Toy animals
Paint
Markers
Construction paper
Glue
Scissors
Sensory bin materials
Blocks
Dress-up clothing
Books
Music player
lessonPlans.vocabularyWords:
Season
Spring
Summer
Fall
Winter
Weather
Rain
Snow
Sunshine
Leaves
Bloom
Temperature
Wind
Nature
lessonPlans.observationOpportunities: Observe children's understanding of seasonal changes, ability to sort and classify items, use of seasonal vocabulary, participation in discussions, and curiosity during investigations.
lessonPlans.adaptations: Provide visual supports and seasonal picture cards. Offer adaptive tools when needed. Allow children to participate through movement, discussion, art, or hands-on exploration.
lessonPlans.familyConnection: Encourage families to discuss seasonal changes they notice outside. Take walks together and observe weather, plants, animals, and clothing choices that relate to the current season.

lessonPlans.title: Kindergarten Readiness
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Children will strengthen the foundational skills needed for kindergarten success through engaging, play-based learning experiences. Throughout the week, children will practice independence, communication, early literacy, math concepts, problem-solving, classroom routines, social skills, and confidence-building activities designed to support a successful transition into kindergarten.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Strengthen letter and name recognition
Develop early math and counting skills
Practice following multi-step directions
Build independence and self-help skills
Strengthen social and emotional readiness
Encourage problem-solving and critical thinking
Develop fine and gross motor coordination
Build confidence in classroom participation

books.title: Miss Bindergarten Gets Ready for Kindergarten
books.author: Joseph Slate

lessonPlans.weeklyMaterials:
Alphabet cards
Name cards
Counting manipulatives
Books

lessonPlans.observationOpportunities: Observe children's independence, ability to follow directions, letter recognition, counting skills, social interactions, problem-solving abilities, and confidence during group activities.
lessonPlans.adaptations: Provide visual schedules and picture supports. Offer adaptive writing tools when needed. Allow children multiple ways to demonstrate learning through movement, discussion, art, and hands-on exploration.
lessonPlans.familyConnection: Encourage children to practice independence skills at home such as cleaning up toys, putting on shoes, washing hands, and following simple routines. Talk positively about kindergarten and new learning opportunities.

lessonPlans.title: Animal Habitats
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Children will become wildlife explorers as they investigate where animals live and why habitats help animals survive. Throughout the week, children will explore forests, oceans, deserts, arctic regions, and jungles through hands-on sensory experiences, dramatic play, STEM building challenges, movement activities, and creative projects. Children will learn how animals adapt to their environments while developing observation, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Identify different animal habitats
Match animals to their habitats
Explore how habitats meet animal needs
Develop scientific observation skills
Strengthen classification and sorting abilities
Build vocabulary related to animals and habitats
Develop fine and gross motor skills
Foster curiosity and respect for wildlife

songs.title: We're Going on a Habitat Hunt

lessonPlans.weeklyMaterials:
Animal figures
Habitat picture cards
Blocks
Artificial plants
Cotton balls
Sand
Blue fabric
Sensory bin fillers
Paint
Markers
Crayons

Glue
Scissors
Magnifying glasses
Books
Music player
lessonPlans.vocabularyWords:

Adapt

lessonPlans.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to match animals to habitats, use habitat vocabulary, classify animals, participate in discussions, solve building challenges, and demonstrate curiosity about wildlife.
lessonPlans.adaptations: Provide visual habitat cards and animal photographs. Offer larger manipulatives when needed. Allow children to demonstrate understanding through movement, art, dramatic play, or verbal discussion.
lessonPlans.familyConnection: Encourage families to discuss where different animals live. Take a nature walk and observe habitats near home. Talk about how people and animals both need food, water, and shelter.

lessonPlans.title: Construction Zone
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Children will become builders, architects, engineers, and construction workers as they explore how things are designed and built. Through hands-on building challenges, dramatic play, measuring activities, construction-themed art, and problem-solving experiences, children will develop teamwork, creativity, and critical thinking skills while learning about the exciting world of construction.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Explore how buildings and structures are created
Develop engineering and problem-solving skills
Practice measuring, counting, and comparing
Strengthen fine and gross motor skills
Build teamwork and communication skills
Learn about construction tools and jobs
Develop creativity through design challenges
Strengthen observation and planning abilities
lessonPlans.weeklyMaterials:
Blocks
Cardboard boxes
Measuring tape
Toy tools
Hard hats
Construction vehicles
Craft sticks
Paper cups
Tape
Paint
Markers
Construction paper
Clipboards
Blueprint examples

Music player
lessonPlans.vocabularyWords:

Blueprint

lessonPlans.observationOpportunities: Observe children's problem-solving skills, ability to work cooperatively, measuring skills, planning abilities, creativity during building activities, and use of construction vocabulary.
lessonPlans.adaptations: Provide larger building materials when needed. Offer visual examples of structures and blueprints. Allow children to participate through building, drawing, dramatic play, or verbal discussion.
lessonPlans.familyConnection: Encourage children to notice buildings, roads, bridges, and construction projects in their community. Talk about how construction workers help build and improve places where people live and work.

lessonPlans.title: Camping Adventure
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Children will become outdoor adventurers as they explore the exciting world of camping through hands-on investigations, dramatic play, nature exploration, storytelling, STEM challenges, and creative activities. Throughout the week, children will learn about camping equipment, wildlife, outdoor safety, nature observation, and teamwork while building confidence and curiosity about the natural world.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Explore camping and outdoor adventure concepts
Learn basic outdoor safety skills
Develop observation and investigation abilities
Strengthen problem-solving and teamwork skills
Practice counting, sorting, and measuring
Build vocabulary related to nature and camping
Strengthen fine and gross motor development
Encourage imaginative and dramatic play
lessonPlans.weeklyMaterials:
Play tent
Flashlights
Binoculars
Nature items
Artificial campfire
Sleeping bags
Toy animals
Magnifying glasses
Blocks
Paint
Markers
Construction paper
Glue
Scissors
Books
Music player
lessonPlans.vocabularyWords:
Camping
Tent
Campfire
Lantern
Trail
Forest
Adventure
Explore
Wildlife
Hiking
Nature
Backpack
Campsite
Ranger
lessonPlans.observationOpportunities: Observe children's cooperation during dramatic play, problem-solving skills, nature observations, vocabulary development, and ability to follow safety guidelines.
lessonPlans.adaptations: Provide visual supports and nature photographs. Allow children multiple ways to participate through movement, art, sensory experiences, dramatic play, or discussion.
lessonPlans.familyConnection: Encourage families to spend time outdoors together. Take a nature walk, observe wildlife, collect leaves, or talk about outdoor adventures and camping experiences.

lessonPlans.title: Little Scientists
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Children will become scientists as they ask questions, make predictions, conduct experiments, observe results, and explore the world around them. Throughout the week, children will investigate colors, magnets, water, plants, and simple chemical reactions while building critical thinking, observation, and problem-solving skills through hands-on discovery.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Develop scientific observation skills
Learn how to make predictions
Explore cause and effect relationships
Practice comparing and classifying objects
Strengthen vocabulary related to science
Build problem-solving and critical thinking skills
Encourage curiosity and questioning
Develop fine and gross motor skills

lessonPlans.title: Amazing Insects
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Children will become insect explorers as they investigate the fascinating world of bugs. Throughout the week, children will discover insect characteristics, life cycles, habitats, pollination, camouflage, and the important roles insects play in nature. Through hands-on investigations, dramatic play, sensory experiences, art, and movement activities, children will develop curiosity and appreciation for these tiny creatures.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Identify common insects and their characteristics
Explore insect habitats and life cycles
Learn about pollination and nature
Develop observation and classification skills
Strengthen counting and comparing abilities
Build scientific vocabulary
Develop fine and gross motor skills
Foster curiosity and respect for living things
lessonPlans.weeklyMaterials:
Plastic insects
Magnifying glasses
Bug viewers
Artificial flowers
Pipe cleaners
Paint
Markers
Construction paper
Play dough
Sensory bin materials
Pom-poms
Clothespins
Books
Music player
lessonPlans.vocabularyWords:
Insect
Antenna
Wings
Thorax
Caterpillar
Butterfly
Bee
Ladybug
Habitat
Pollinate
Cocoon
Camouflage
Larva
Metamorphosis
lessonPlans.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to identify insects, classify bugs, describe insect features, participate in investigations, and demonstrate curiosity about living things.
lessonPlans.adaptations: Provide insect photographs and visual supports. Offer larger manipulatives when needed. Allow children to participate through observation, movement, art, or dramatic play.
lessonPlans.familyConnection: Encourage families to look for insects outdoors. Observe butterflies, ants, bees, or ladybugs and discuss how insects help plants and nature.

Develop creative problem-solving skills
Learn about inventors and inventions

Strengthen engineering and building skills
Build confidence in sharing ideas
Develop teamwork and cooperation

lessonPlans.title: Archaeology Adventure
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Children will become archaeologists as they dig for artifacts, uncover fossils, investigate ancient discoveries, and explore how people learn about the past. Through hands-on excavation activities, dramatic play, sensory exploration, art projects, and STEM challenges, children will develop curiosity, observation skills, and a love for discovery.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Learn what archaeologists do
Explore fossils and artifacts
Develop observation and investigation skills
Practice sorting, classifying, and measuring
Strengthen fine and gross motor skills
Build vocabulary related to archaeology
Encourage problem-solving and critical thinking
Foster curiosity about history and discovery

songs.title: We're Going on a Fossil Hunt

lessonPlans.familyConnection: Encourage children to look for interesting rocks, shells, and natural objects outdoors. Discuss how people learn about the past by studying clues and discoveries.

lessonPlans.title: Gardening & Plant Life
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Children will become gardeners and plant scientists as they explore seeds, flowers, vegetables, insects, plant life cycles, and the needs of living things. Through hands-on planting experiences, sensory exploration, dramatic play, art, STEM investigations, and nature observations, children will discover how plants grow and why gardens are important.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Identify the parts of a plant
Explore plant life cycles
Learn what plants need to grow
Develop observation and investigation skills
Practice counting, sorting, and measuring
Strengthen fine and gross motor skills
Build vocabulary related to gardening
Foster responsibility through plant care
lessonPlans.weeklyMaterials:
Seeds
Soil
Plant pots
Watering cans
Flowers
Vegetables
Magnifying glasses
Gardening gloves
Artificial plants
Paint
Markers
Construction paper
Glue
Scissors
Books
Music player
lessonPlans.vocabularyWords:
Seed
Plant
Flower
Stem
Roots
Leaf
Garden
Soil
Water
Sunlight
Grow
Sprout
Vegetable
Harvest
lessonPlans.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to identify plant parts, describe plant growth, care for living things, use scientific vocabulary, and participate in gardening activities.
lessonPlans.adaptations: Provide larger gardening tools when needed. Use visual plant life cycle cards. Allow children to participate through planting, observation, art, dramatic play, or discussion.
lessonPlans.familyConnection: Encourage families to plant flowers, herbs, or vegetables together. Observe plants growing around your home and discuss what helps them stay healthy.

lessonPlans.title: Pet Pals
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Children will explore the wonderful world of pets while learning about responsibility, kindness, animal care, and pet habitats. Through hands-on investigations, dramatic play, sensory experiences, art projects, movement activities, and early science concepts, children will discover how pets depend on people for food, shelter, love, and care.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Identify common household pets
Learn how to care for animals responsibly
Develop empathy and kindness toward living things
Explore pet needs and habitats
Strengthen observation and classification skills
Build vocabulary related to animals and pet care
Develop fine and gross motor skills
Foster responsibility and cooperation

lessonPlans.title: Zoo Adventure
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Children will become zoo explorers as they investigate animals from around the world. Through hands-on discovery, dramatic play, movement activities, sensory experiences, art projects, and STEM challenges, children will learn about animal habitats, diets, behaviors, and the important role zoos play in conservation and animal care.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Identify a variety of zoo animals
Explore animal habitats and needs
Learn about animal care and conservation
Develop observation and classification skills
Practice counting, sorting, and comparing
Strengthen fine and gross motor skills
Build vocabulary related to animals and habitats
Foster curiosity and respect for wildlife
lessonPlans.weeklyMaterials:
Zoo animal figures
Animal habitat pictures
Blocks
Magnifying glasses
Binoculars
Toy veterinarian kit
Animal masks
Paint
Markers
Construction paper
Glue
Scissors
Sensory bin materials
Books
Music player
lessonPlans.vocabularyWords:
Zoo
Habitat
Conservation
Keeper
Veterinarian
Mammal
Reptile
Bird
Exhibit
Safari
Wildlife
Endangered
Species
Animal Care
lessonPlans.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to identify animals, classify animals by habitat or type, use new vocabulary, participate in dramatic play, and demonstrate curiosity during investigations.
lessonPlans.adaptations: Provide animal picture cards and visual supports. Offer larger manipulatives when needed. Allow children to participate through movement, art, dramatic play, sensory exploration, or discussion.
lessonPlans.familyConnection: Encourage families to visit a zoo, nature center, or wildlife park if possible. Discuss favorite animals and how people can help protect wildlife and habitats.

lessonPlans.title: Zoo Adventures
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Toddlers will spend the week exploring exciting zoo animals through movement, sensory experiences, dramatic play, art, music, and hands-on investigations. lessonPlans.title: Camping Under the Stars
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Toddlers will explore the fun of camping through pretend campfires, nature discoveries, animal adventures, outdoor-inspired sensory experiences, and imaginative play. Children will learn about nature, nighttime, friendship, exploration, and outdoor safety while building language, motor, and social-emotional skills.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Explore camping and outdoor experiences.
Learn about nature and forest animals.
Develop imagination through dramatic play.
Strengthen gross and fine motor skills.
Practice observation and exploration skills.
Build vocabulary related to camping.
Encourage teamwork and cooperative play.

items.objective: Practice open-ended exploration skills during Flashlight Exploration.
items.description: Toddlers explore Flashlight Exploration during our Camping Under the Stars week through open-ended exploration.
items.materials:
flashlights
Theme toys/figurines
Baskets
Picture cards
items.setup: Prepare a toddler-ready space and materials for Flashlight Exploration.
items.steps:
1. Invite toddlers to explore Flashlight Exploration with hands-on materials related to Camping Under the Stars.
2. Stay nearby and narrate what children notice using simple theme words.
3. Offer choices and follow each child's interest for a few minutes at a time.
4. Encourage pointing, naming, and short conversations about discoveries.
items.teacherRole: Observe, narrate discoveries, and introduce theme vocabulary without directing every action.
learningGoals: Engage in Flashlight Exploration through toddler-friendly open-ended exploration.
Use theme vocabulary related to Camping Under the Stars.
Practice social interaction, curiosity, and motor skills during play.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe engagement, theme vocabulary, motor skills, and social interaction.
items.adaptations: Offer larger materials, hand-over-hand support, and a shorter turn. Allow parallel play instead of forced sharing.
items.safetyNotes: Supervise closely, keep materials too large to choke on, and clear walkways for active movement. Check outdoor surfaces before play.

lessonPlans.title: Construction Crew
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Toddlers will become builders, engineers, and construction workers as they explore trucks, tools, building materials, and creative construction projects. Throughout the week children will build structures, move materials, investigate how things are made, and develop teamwork skills through hands-on play experiences.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Explore construction vehicles and tools.
Practice building and problem-solving skills.
Strengthen fine and gross motor development.
Develop teamwork and cooperative play.
Build vocabulary related to construction.
Investigate cause and effect through building activities.
Encourage creativity and persistence.
lessonPlans.weeklyMaterials:
Blocks
cardboard boxes
toy trucks
toy tools
hard hats
measuring tapes
paint
construction paper
sensory bin filler
toy cones
play dough
craft sticks
tape
large building bricks
toy wheelbarrows
foam blocks
safety vests
clipboards.
lessonPlans.vocabularyWords:
Construction
Builder
Hammer
Truck
Crane
Bulldozer
Dump Truck
Hard Hat
Measure
Build
Lift
Stack
Site
Tools
Engineer
lessonPlans.observationOpportunities: Observe problem-solving skills, persistence, teamwork, vocabulary growth, fine motor development, and creativity during building activities.
lessonPlans.adaptations: Provide larger building materials, adaptive tools, visual supports, and opportunities for individual or group participation.
lessonPlans.familyConnection: Invite families to point out construction projects, trucks, or buildings in their community and discuss what workers do to help build them.

lessonPlans.title: Pet Vet Clinic
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Toddlers will become caring veterinarians as they learn about pets, animal care, kindness, and responsibility. Children will engage in dramatic play, hands-on investigations, movement activities, and creative experiences while exploring what pets need to stay healthy and happy.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Learn about common household pets.
Practice caring and nurturing behaviors.
Develop empathy and social-emotional skills.
Build vocabulary related to animals and pet care.
Strengthen fine and gross motor skills.
Encourage imaginative play and problem-solving.
Explore basic animal needs and routines.

books.title: Pete the Cat and the New Guy

songs.title: How Much Is That Doggie in the Window?

lessonPlans.adaptations: Offer sensory-friendly materials, larger dramatic play tools, visual supports, and flexible participation opportunities.
lessonPlans.familyConnection: Invite families to share photos of pets or discuss animals children have interacted with. Encourage children to talk about how animals are cared for at home.

lessonPlans.title: Bugs & Butterflies
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Toddlers will become little nature explorers as they investigate bugs, butterflies, caterpillars, and other tiny creatures. Through sensory play, movement, art, dramatic play, and hands-on discovery, children will develop curiosity about the natural world while strengthening observation, language, and motor skills.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Explore common insects and bugs.
Observe similarities and differences between insects.
Learn about butterfly life cycles.
Strengthen observation and discovery skills.
Develop fine and gross motor coordination.
Build nature-related vocabulary.
Encourage curiosity and respect for living things.
lessonPlans.weeklyMaterials:
Bug figurines
butterfly models
magnifying glasses
bug catchers
play dough
paint
coffee filters
pipe cleaners
sensory bin materials
leaves
flowers
grass clippings
insect books
butterfly stickers
nature photos
baskets
bug nets
construction paper
crayons.
lessonPlans.vocabularyWords:
Bug
Butterfly
Caterpillar
Cocoon
Wings
Ant
Ladybug
Bee
Nature
Garden
Crawl
Fly
Explore
Insect
Pollinate
lessonPlans.observationOpportunities: Observe curiosity, language development, fine motor skills, nature exploration, scientific thinking, and participation in group activities.
lessonPlans.adaptations: Provide larger bug models, visual supports, sensory alternatives, and opportunities for children to participate at their own comfort level.
lessonPlans.familyConnection: Encourage families to take nature walks and look for bugs, butterflies, and insects outdoors. Invite children to share their discoveries with classmates.

lessonPlans.title: Superhero Training Camp
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Toddlers will become everyday superheroes as they explore kindness, helping others, courage, problem-solving, teamwork, and healthy habits through imaginative play. Throughout the week children will complete superhero missions, obstacle courses, rescue challenges, and creative activities while building confidence and social-emotional skills.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Practice kindness and helping behaviors.
Develop confidence and self-expression.
Strengthen gross and fine motor skills.
Encourage teamwork and cooperation.
Build problem-solving abilities.
Expand vocabulary related to emotions and community.
Engage in imaginative dramatic play.

items.description: Toddlers explore Super Badge Creation during our Superhero Training Camp week through fine motor.
items.materials:
Play dough or crayons
Small manipulatives
Paper
items.setup: Prepare a toddler-ready space and materials for Super Badge Creation.
items.steps:
1. Offer materials for Super Badge Creation that invite pinching, placing, sticking, or scribbling.
2. Demonstrate one simple action, then invite toddlers to try.
3. Celebrate effort and keep tools large enough for little hands.
4. Support turn-taking when children want the same material.
items.teacherRole: Offer hand-over-hand support when wanted and keep materials accessible on low trays.
learningGoals: Engage in Super Badge Creation through toddler-friendly fine motor.
Use theme vocabulary related to Superhero Training Camp.
Practice social interaction, curiosity, and motor skills during play.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe engagement, theme vocabulary, motor skills, and social interaction.
items.adaptations: Offer larger materials, hand-over-hand support, and a shorter turn. Allow parallel play instead of forced sharing.
items.safetyNotes: Supervise closely, keep materials too large to choke on, and clear walkways for active movement. Check outdoor surfaces before play.

lessonPlans.title: Pirate Adventure
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Toddlers will set sail on an exciting pirate adventure filled with treasure hunts, map exploration, ocean discoveries, teamwork challenges, and imaginative play. Throughout the week children will build pirate ships, search for treasure, explore movement activities, and develop problem-solving skills while engaging in hands-on learning.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Encourage imaginative and dramatic play.
Develop problem-solving and exploration skills.
Strengthen gross and fine motor development.
Practice teamwork and cooperation.
Expand vocabulary through themed play.
Explore maps, directions, and simple navigation concepts.
Build confidence through adventure-based learning.
lessonPlans.weeklyMaterials:
Pirate hats
treasure chests
gold coins
cardboard boxes
toy boats
scarves
maps
sensory bin materials
magnifying glasses
blocks
paint
crayons
stickers
construction paper
toy telescopes
gems
sand
buckets
pirate-themed books.
lessonPlans.vocabularyWords:
Pirate
Treasure
Ship
Map
Ocean
Island
Captain
Sail
Adventure
Gold
Chest
Search
Explore
Crew
Telescope
lessonPlans.observationOpportunities: Observe imaginative play, communication skills, cooperation, problem-solving, gross motor development, and curiosity during exploration activities.
lessonPlans.adaptations: Provide larger materials, visual supports, sensory-friendly options, and opportunities for individual participation.
lessonPlans.familyConnection: Encourage families to create simple treasure hunts at home or talk about adventures and exploration with their child.

lessonPlans.title: Welcome to My Classroom
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Welcome to My Classroom helps toddlers build confidence and feel secure as they begin a new school year. Throughout the week, children will become familiar with their classroom, meet teachers and classmates, practice simple routines, and explore learning centers through hands-on play. Activities encourage social interaction, independence, communication, and a sense of belonging while helping children develop positive feelings about coming to school.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Become familiar with the classroom environment.
Build trusting relationships with teachers.
Practice simple classroom routines.
Learn classmates' names.
Explore classroom learning centers.
Increase confidence and independence.
Express feelings about school.
Practice listening and following simple directions.

books.title: Llama Llama Misses Mama by Anna Dewdney
The Kissing Hand by Audrey Penn
Pete the Kitty's First Day of Preschool by James Dean
Maisy Goes to Preschool by Lucy Cousins
David Goes to School by David Shannon

lessonPlans.observationOpportunities:
Observe how children separate from caregivers.
Observe participation in classroom routines.
Observe interactions with teachers and peers.
Observe communication skills during play.
Observe exploration of learning centers.
Observe ability to follow one-step directions.
Observe confidence during transitions.
Observe curiosity and engagement throughout the day.
lessonPlans.adaptations:
Provide a visual daily schedule.
Offer comfort items or family photos when appropriate.
Allow extra transition time for children who need it.
Use simple one-step directions with visual cues.
Pair hesitant children with a supportive peer or teacher.
Offer sensory breaks as needed.
Adapt materials for varying developmental levels and physical abilities.
Celebrate each child's progress and participation at their own pace.
lessonPlans.familyConnection: Invite families to talk with their child about school each evening. Encourage children to share one favorite activity from their day and, if possible, bring a small family photo to display in the classroom. Share positive updates during the first week to help families feel connected and reassure children as they adjust to their new classroom routine.

items.title: Hello, Friends!
items.objective: Help children learn classmates' names and feel welcomed.
items.description: Children sit in a circle while greeting one another with smiles, waves, and simple introductions.
items.setup: Have children sit in a circle with their name tags on.
items.steps:
1. Welcome each child by name.
2. Encourage everyone to wave hello.
3. Sing the Hello Song together.
4. Let each child say or hear their name.
5. Celebrate everyone's participation with claps.
items.teacherRole: Model greetings, encourage participation, and reassure children who may be nervous.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe eye contact, participation, and comfort level with peers.
items.adaptations: Allow children to wave instead of speaking if they are shy.
items.safetyNotes: Provide enough personal space for all children during circle time.

items.title: Classroom Treasure Hunt

items.description: Children explore learning centers while teachers explain what happens in each area.
items.materials:

Learning center materials
items.setup: Prepare each learning center before children arrive.
items.steps:
1. Walk together around the classroom.
2. Stop at each learning center.
3. Explain what children can do there.
4. Allow children to explore briefly.
5. Praise safe choices and curiosity.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe curiosity, attention, and willingness to explore.
items.adaptations: Allow extra time for hesitant children.
items.safetyNotes: Keep walkways clear and supervise children closely.

Glue sticks

items.steps:
1. Give each child a paper.
2. Encourage coloring.
3. Add stickers.
4. Write each child's name on their artwork.
5. Display artwork in the classroom.
items.teacherRole: Encourage creativity and celebrate each child's work.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe grip strength and participation.
items.adaptations: Offer larger crayons or adaptive grips if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Use only non-toxic art supplies.

items.safetyNotes: Provide plenty of space for safe movement.

lessonPlans.title: My Feelings at School
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: My Feelings at School helps toddlers recognize, name, and express their emotions in healthy ways while adjusting to the school environment. Throughout the week, children will explore feelings such as happy, sad, excited, frustrated, scared, and calm through stories, dramatic play, art, music, and hands-on activities. They will practice identifying emotions in themselves and others, learn simple calming strategies, and build empathy, kindness, and confidence as they develop positive relationships with teachers and classmates.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Identify and name common emotions.
Express feelings using words, facial expressions, and actions.
Develop empathy for classmates.
Learn simple calming strategies.
Build confidence and emotional security at school.
Strengthen communication skills.
Practice problem-solving during social situations.
Build positive friendships and classroom relationships.

books.title: The Color Monster by Anna Llenas
Today I Feel Silly by Jamie Lee Curtis
Glad Monster, Sad Monster by Ed Emberley & Anne Miranda
Llama Llama Misses Mama by Anna Dewdney

items.title: Tear and Glue Feelings Heart
items.objective: Express emotions through a calming art activity.
items.description: Children tear red tissue paper into small pieces and glue them onto a heart while talking about healthy ways to calm down when upset.
items.materials:
Heart templates
Red tissue paper
Glue sticks
Crayons
items.setup: Prepare heart templates before the activity.
items.steps:
1. Give each child a heart template.
2. Tear tissue paper into small pieces.
3. Glue pieces onto the heart.
4. Decorate with crayons.
5. Share one thing that helps you feel calm.
items.teacherRole: Encourage emotional conversations while assisting with fine motor skills.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe participation and ability to discuss calming ideas.
items.adaptations: Offer pre-cut paper or larger pieces if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Closely supervise glue and art materials.

items.title: Pinwheel Breathing
items.objective: Teach deep breathing as a calming strategy.
items.description: Children practice slow, controlled breathing by blowing pinwheels.
items.setup: Seat children comfortably in a circle.
items.steps:
1. Hold the pinwheel.
2. Take a slow deep breath.
3. Blow gently to make it spin.
4. Repeat several times.
5. Watch the calm-down bottle settle.
items.teacherRole: Model slow breathing and praise children's efforts.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to participate in calming exercises.
items.adaptations: Use bubbles instead of pinwheels if preferred.
items.safetyNotes: Remind children not to place pinwheels in their mouths.

items.title: Helping the Mad Monster
items.objective: Practice problem-solving and empathy.
items.description: A puppet feels angry because something didn't go its way. Children suggest safe ways to help the puppet calm down.
items.materials:
Monster puppet
Stuffed animals
Emotion cards
items.setup: Create a small puppet stage.
items.steps:
1. Introduce the angry puppet.
2. Ask what happened.
3. Brainstorm ways to help.
4. Practice deep breathing with the puppet.
5. Celebrate when the puppet feels calm.
items.teacherRole: Guide children toward healthy coping strategies and respectful communication.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to suggest calming strategies and show empathy.
items.adaptations: Offer visual calming cards or sentence starters.
items.safetyNotes: Use soft puppets and supervise dramatic play.

thursday.theme: I Can Feel Scared and Be Brave
thursday.objectives:
Identify the feeling of being scared or nervous.
Understand that everyone feels scared sometimes.
Learn healthy ways to feel safe and brave.
Build trust with teachers and classmates.
Practice asking for help when needed.
thursday.materials:
Emotion picture cards
Feelings chart
Handheld mirrors
Stuffed animals
Puppets
Blankets
Flashlights
Cardboard boxes or play tunnel
Construction paper
Yellow star stickers
Crayons
Music player
Calm-down bottle
thursday.vocabulary:
Scared
Brave
Safe
Help
Comfort
Courage

items.title: Brave Faces
items.objective: Help children recognize and talk about feeling scared.
items.description: Children use mirrors to make scared and brave faces while discussing situations that might make someone nervous.
items.setup: Sit together in a circle.
items.steps:
1. Show the scared emotion card.
2. Make a scared face together.
3. Look in the mirrors.
4. Practice changing the scared face into a brave smile.
5. Talk about who helps us feel safe.
items.teacherRole: Provide reassurance and encourage children to share experiences if they feel comfortable.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to recognize fear and identify trusted adults.
items.adaptations: Allow children to point to emotion cards instead of speaking.
items.safetyNotes: Use child-safe mirrors and supervise appropriately.

items.title: Helping Teddy Feel Brave
items.objective: Develop empathy and problem-solving skills.
items.description: Children comfort a teddy bear that feels scared and suggest ways to help it feel safe.
items.setup: Create a cozy comfort corner.
items.steps:
1. Introduce Teddy, who feels scared.
2. Ask children how they can help.
3. Wrap Teddy in a blanket or give a gentle pat.
4. Practice saying kind words like, "You're safe."
5. Celebrate helping Teddy feel brave.
items.teacherRole: Model empathy, kindness, and reassuring language.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe caring behaviors and emotional understanding.
items.adaptations: Model responses or offer visual choices for children needing support.
items.safetyNotes: Respect children's personal space and encourage asking permission before hugs.

items.title: Brave Adventure Course
items.objective: Build confidence while trying new challenges.
items.description: Children complete a simple obstacle course while teachers and classmates cheer them on.
items.materials:
Tunnels
Floor spots
Cones
Balance beam or tape line
items.setup: Create a safe obstacle course with plenty of space.
items.steps:
1. Demonstrate each obstacle.
2. Encourage children to try one step at a time.
3. Cheer for each classmate.
4. Celebrate every accomplishment.
5. Talk about how trying something new can make us feel brave.
items.teacherRole: Provide encouragement and assist children when needed.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe willingness to try new activities and ask for help.
items.adaptations: Modify obstacles based on each child's ability.
items.safetyNotes: Closely supervise all climbing and balancing activities.

items.title: My Brave Star
items.objective: Celebrate courage and confidence.
items.description: Children decorate a large star representing something brave they did today.
items.setup: Prepare star templates before the activity.
items.steps:
1. Give each child a star.
2. Decorate with crayons and stickers.
3. Talk about one brave thing they did today.
4. Write each child's words on the star.
5. Display the stars on a "Brave at School" bulletin board.
items.teacherRole: Celebrate every child's effort and encourage positive self-talk.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe participation and confidence while sharing.
items.adaptations: Offer adaptive art tools or teacher assistance as needed.
items.safetyNotes: Use only child-safe art supplies.

friday.objectives:
Review the emotions learned throughout the week.
Identify happy, sad, mad, scared, and calm feelings.
Demonstrate healthy ways to express emotions.
Celebrate emotional growth and friendships.
Build confidence using feeling words.
friday.materials:
Emotion picture cards
Feelings chart
Handheld mirrors
Puppets
Stuffed animals
Construction paper
Crayons
Stickers
Emotion sorting cards
Music player
Scarves
Bean bags
Calm-down bottle
"Feelings Superstar" certificates (optional)
friday.vocabulary:
Happy
Sad
Mad
Scared
Calm
Proud
Feelings
Friend
Kind
Brave

items.title: Feelings Match-Up
items.objective: Review and identify multiple emotions.
items.description: Children match emotion cards to the correct facial expressions and talk about situations when someone might feel each emotion.
items.setup: Spread emotion cards on the floor in a circle.
items.steps:
1. Show an emotion card.
2. Ask children to name the feeling.
3. Match the card to the Feelings Chart.
4. Make the matching facial expression.
5. Talk about one time someone might feel that emotion.
items.teacherRole: Encourage discussion and reinforce that every feeling is okay.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to identify and describe emotions.
items.adaptations: Provide visual choices or simplify to two emotions at a time if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Ensure cards remain clean and free from slipping hazards.

items.title: My Feelings Wheel
items.objective: Create a visual reminder of different emotions.
items.description: Children decorate a feelings wheel showing happy, sad, mad, scared, and calm faces.
items.materials:
Feelings wheel template
Crayons
Markers
Stickers
Paper fastener (teacher assembly)
items.setup: Prepare wheel templates before the activity.
items.steps:
1. Color each emotion.
2. Talk about each feeling.
3. Assemble the wheel with teacher assistance.
4. Spin the wheel and name the feeling.
5. Take the wheel home to share with family.
items.teacherRole: Support children while encouraging conversations about emotions.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe understanding of different emotions and participation.
items.adaptations: Provide pre-colored examples or adaptive crayons as needed.
items.safetyNotes: Teacher should assemble wheels using paper fasteners.

items.title: Feelings Freeze Dance
items.objective: Express emotions through movement.
items.description: Children dance while music plays. When the music stops, the teacher holds up an emotion card and children freeze showing that feeling with their face and body.
items.setup: Clear a large open movement area.
items.steps:
1. Dance while music plays.
2. Freeze when the music stops.
3. Show the emotion on the card.
4. Talk briefly about the feeling.
5. Repeat using different emotions.
items.teacherRole: Model facial expressions and encourage participation.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe emotional recognition and body control.
items.adaptations: Allow seated participation or simplified movements.
items.safetyNotes: Maintain safe spacing between children during movement.

items.title: Feelings Superstar Celebration
items.objective: Celebrate each child's emotional growth throughout the week.
items.description: Children receive recognition for learning about feelings and practicing kindness, bravery, and healthy emotional expression.
items.setup: Arrange children in a circle.
items.steps:
1. Review the week's emotions.
2. Call each child by name.
3. Share one positive thing the child practiced this week.
4. Present a certificate or sticker.
5. End with a class cheer and group photo if permission has been provided.
items.teacherRole: Celebrate every child's growth while building confidence and belonging.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe confidence, peer encouragement, and participation.
items.adaptations: Present recognition individually for children who prefer less attention.
items.safetyNotes: Ensure children remain seated while waiting for their turn.

lessonPlans.title: Amazing Apples
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: This week, toddlers will explore the wonderful world of apples through hands-on investigations, sensory experiences, movement, music, dramatic play, art, and early science activities. Children will discover that apples come in different colors, sizes, and tastes while learning where apples grow and how they become healthy foods we can enjoy. Throughout the week, they will strengthen language skills, early math concepts, fine and gross motor development, and social-emotional skills by working together during engaging apple-themed experiences.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Identify apples as a healthy fruit.
Recognize red, green, and yellow apples.
Explore apples using the five senses.
Compare apples by size, color, and texture.
Practice counting, sorting, and matching apples.
Strengthen fine motor skills through art and sensory play.
Build vocabulary related to apples and orchards.
Encourage curiosity through simple science investigations.
Participate in cooperative play and group discussions.
Develop confidence while exploring new foods and experiences.

songs.title: Way Up High in the Apple Tree
If You're Happy and You Know It (Apple Version)

lessonPlans.adaptations:
Provide adaptive scissors and crayons as needed.
Use picture cards for vocabulary support.
Offer larger manipulatives for children needing additional assistance.
Modify activities based on developmental levels.
lessonPlans.familyConnection: Invite families to visit a grocery store or orchard together to look for different apples. Encourage children to taste apples at home and talk about their favorite color, taste, and texture.

monday.objectives:
Identify an apple by sight and touch.
Explore apples using the five senses.
Recognize red, green, and yellow apples.
Build apple-related vocabulary.
Practice early counting skills.
monday.materials:
Red, green, and yellow apples
Apple basket
Magnifying glasses
Apple picture cards
Apple slices
Chart paper

items.title: Apple Investigation
items.objective: Introduce children to observing apples using their five senses.
items.description: Children investigate real apples by looking, touching, smelling, and listening while learning descriptive vocabulary.
items.materials:
Red, green, and yellow apples
Magnifying glasses
items.setup: Place apples in the center of the table with magnifying glasses nearby.
items.steps:
1. Give each child an apple.
2. Look closely using magnifying glasses.
3. Feel the smooth skin.
4. Smell the apple.
5. Tap gently and listen to the sound.
6. Talk about what everyone noticed.
items.teacherRole: Encourage observation by asking open-ended questions and introducing new vocabulary.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe children's willingness to explore and describe the apples.
items.adaptations: Provide larger apples or additional teacher support as needed.
items.safetyNotes: Closely supervise children while handling real apples.

items.title: Apple Stamp Painting
items.objective: Explore color while creating apple artwork.
items.description: Children use apple halves dipped in paint to create colorful apple prints.
items.materials:
Apple halves
Red, green, and yellow paint
White construction paper
Smocks
items.setup: Cut apples in half before the activity and pour paint into shallow trays.
items.steps:
1. Dip the apple into paint.
2. Press onto paper.
3. Lift carefully.
4. Repeat using different colors.
5. Allow artwork to dry for display.
items.teacherRole: Model stamping techniques and encourage color recognition.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe hand control and participation.
items.adaptations: Provide sponge stamps if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Use only non-toxic washable paint and supervise closely.

items.title: Count the Apples
items.objective: Practice one-to-one counting.
items.description: Children count plastic apples and place them into baskets.
items.materials:
Plastic apples
Small baskets
Number cards 1–5
items.setup: Place apples beside empty baskets.
items.steps:
1. Choose a number card.
2. Count the correct number of apples.
3. Place apples into the basket.
4. Count together.
5. Repeat with another number.
items.teacherRole: Model counting slowly and encourage children to touch each apple as they count.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe counting accuracy and participation.
items.adaptations: Reduce the number of apples or provide hand-over-hand assistance.
items.safetyNotes: Use large manipulatives to prevent choking hazards.

items.title: Pick the Apples
items.objective: Develop gross motor skills while reinforcing apple vocabulary.
items.description: Children pretend to reach high into an apple tree, pick apples, place them in baskets, and carry them to the pretend orchard.
items.materials:
Music player
Apple baskets
Plastic apples
items.setup: Scatter plastic apples around the classroom.
items.steps:
1. Play apple-themed music.
2. Pretend to reach high into the tree.
3. Pick an apple.
4. Carry it to the basket.
5. Repeat until all apples have been collected.
items.teacherRole: Encourage movement, counting, and imaginative play.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe balance, coordination, and participation.
items.adaptations: Place apples within easy reach or allow seated participation if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Ensure children walk while carrying apples and keep the activity area free of obstacles.

tuesday.objectives:
Identify red, green, and yellow apples.
Compare apples by color.
Practice sorting and matching.

Expand apple vocabulary.

items.title: Apple Color Sort
items.objective: Develop color recognition and sorting skills.
items.description: Children sort apples into matching colored baskets while practicing color vocabulary.
items.materials:
Plastic apples
Red basket
Green basket
Yellow basket
items.setup: Mix all apples together in one large basket.
items.steps:
1. Show each colored basket.
2. Pick up one apple.
3. Name its color.
4. Place it into the matching basket.
5. Count how many apples are in each basket.
items.teacherRole: Encourage children to say each color aloud while sorting.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to identify and sort colors correctly.
items.adaptations: Use only two colors if children need a simpler activity.
items.safetyNotes: Use large manipulatives appropriate for toddlers.

items.title: My Favorite Apple Color
items.objective: Explore colors through creative expression.
items.description: Children create a colorful apple collage using tissue paper, paint, and stickers.
items.materials:
Apple templates
Red, green, and yellow tissue paper
Glue sticks
Stickers
Crayons
items.setup: Prepare apple templates before the activity.
items.steps:
1. Choose a favorite apple color.
2. Glue tissue paper onto the apple.
3. Decorate with crayons and stickers.
4. Share your favorite apple color.
5. Display artwork around the classroom.
items.teacherRole: Encourage creativity while reinforcing color names.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe color choices and participation.
items.adaptations: Offer larger tissue paper pieces or sponge painting.
items.safetyNotes: Closely supervise glue and art materials.

items.title: Apple Color Investigation
items.objective: Compare apples by observing their colors and features.
items.description: Children closely examine apples to discover that apples can be different colors while still being the same fruit.
items.setup: Arrange apples on a science table.
items.steps:
1. Observe each apple.
2. Compare the colors.
3. Feel the apples.
4. Talk about what is the same and different.
5. Decide which apple is your favorite.
items.teacherRole: Ask open-ended questions and encourage careful observation.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe curiosity and descriptive language.
items.adaptations: Allow children to work with a partner.
items.safetyNotes: Inspect apples before handling.

items.title: Apple Color Dance
items.objective: Reinforce color recognition through movement.
items.description: Children dance while holding colorful scarves. When the music stops, the teacher calls a color and children find the matching apple.
items.materials:
Music player
Color scarves
Plastic apples
items.setup: Scatter apples throughout the room.
items.steps:
1. Dance with scarves.
2. Freeze when the music stops.
3. Listen for a color.
4. Find the matching apple.
5. Repeat with different colors.
items.teacherRole: Encourage movement and celebrate successful color matching.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe listening, coordination, and color identification.
items.adaptations: Reduce the number of colors or provide teacher guidance.
items.safetyNotes: Keep the movement area clear and remind children to walk while finding apples.

wednesday.objectives:
Compare apples by size.
Recognize that apples are round.
Use comparison words like big, small, larger, and smaller.
Practice measuring and sorting.
Strengthen observation and problem-solving skills.

Large, medium, and small apples
Plastic apples
Measuring tape

Apple picture cards

items.title: Big or Small?
items.objective: Develop comparison and classification skills.
items.description: Children compare apples by size and sort them into "Big" and "Small" baskets.
items.materials:
Large apples
Small apples
Two baskets
Size labels
items.setup: Mix apples together in one large basket.
items.steps:
1. Show the two baskets.
2. Pick up one apple.
3. Decide if it is big or small.
4. Place it into the correct basket.
5. Count the apples in each basket.
items.teacherRole: Model comparison words and encourage children to explain their thinking.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to compare sizes and classify objects.
items.adaptations: Begin with only two noticeably different sizes before introducing medium apples.
items.safetyNotes: Use age-appropriate apples and supervise closely.

items.title: Apple Measuring Station
items.objective: Introduce simple measurement concepts.
items.description: Children explore how apples can be measured using yarn, measuring tape, or linking cubes.
items.materials:
Apples
Measuring tape
Yarn
Linking cubes
items.setup: Arrange measuring materials on a science table.
items.steps:
1. Choose an apple.
2. Wrap yarn around the apple.
3. Compare the yarn lengths.
4. Count linking cubes if using them.
5. Talk about which apple is bigger.
items.teacherRole: Introduce simple measurement vocabulary while encouraging exploration.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe curiosity and understanding of measurement.
items.adaptations: Use only one measuring tool if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Closely supervise measuring materials.

items.title: Round Apple Collage
items.objective: Recognize the round shape of an apple.
items.description: Children create a collage using paper circles to build colorful apples.
items.materials:
Red, green, and yellow paper circles
Glue sticks
Construction paper
Crayons
Brown and green paper strips
items.setup: Prepare paper circles and stems before the activity.
items.steps:
1. Choose a paper circle.
2. Glue it onto the paper.
3. Add a stem and leaf.
4. Decorate the background.
5. Share your apple with the class.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe shape recognition and fine motor skills.
items.adaptations: Offer larger paper pieces or pre-glued examples.
items.safetyNotes: Use child-safe scissors only if needed with close supervision.

items.title: Roll Like an Apple
items.objective: Develop body awareness and gross motor skills.
items.description: Children pretend to be apples by curling into a ball, rolling carefully on mats, stretching into apple trees, and reaching high to pick pretend apples.
items.materials:
Gym mats
Music player
Bean bags
items.setup: Create a large open movement area with mats.
items.steps:
1. Pretend to grow into an apple tree.
2. Reach up high.
3. Curl into a round apple.
4. Carefully roll across the mat.
5. Stand up and pretend to place your apple into a basket.
items.teacherRole: Model each movement and encourage safe participation.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe balance, coordination, and participation.
items.adaptations: Allow children to perform movements while seated or with teacher assistance.
items.safetyNotes: Use mats on a flat surface and supervise rolling activities closely.

thursday.objectives:
Explore apples using the sense of taste.
Describe apples using simple descriptive words.
Compare different apple varieties.
Practice making predictions.
Encourage trying new healthy foods.
thursday.materials:
Red apples
Green apples
Yellow apples
Small tasting plates
Child-safe knives (teacher use only)
Napkins
Apple graph
Apple picture cards
Chart paper
Stickers
Play food apples
Music player
Apple basket
thursday.vocabulary:
Taste
Sweet
Crunchy

items.title: Apple Taste Test
items.objective: Explore different apple varieties using the sense of taste.
items.description: Children sample small pieces of red, green, and yellow apples while comparing their flavors and textures.
items.materials:
Red apples
Green apples
Yellow apples
Small plates
Napkins
items.setup: Wash and slice apples before children arrive. Place one slice of each apple on every plate.
items.steps:
1. Look at each apple.
2. Smell each apple.
3. Taste one slice at a time.
4. Talk about which apple tastes sweet, tart, or crunchy.
5. Choose your favorite apple.
items.teacherRole: Encourage children to describe what they taste while respecting that everyone may have different preferences.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe children's willingness to try new foods and describe their experiences.
items.adaptations: Offer only one apple variety if children are hesitant or have sensory sensitivities.
items.safetyNotes: Always check for food allergies. Cut apples into small bite-sized pieces and supervise closely during tasting.

items.title: Favorite Apple Graph
items.objective: Introduce simple graphing and counting skills.
items.description: Children place their name or sticker above their favorite apple color to create a classroom graph.
items.materials:
Large graph paper
Apple color pictures
Name cards or stickers
items.setup: Prepare a graph with three columns labeled Red, Green, and Yellow.
items.steps:
1. Decide your favorite apple.
2. Find the matching column.
3. Place your sticker.
4. Count each column together.
5. Discover which apple was the class favorite.
items.teacherRole: Guide children through counting and comparing which column has the most and least.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe counting skills and ability to interpret simple graphs.
items.adaptations: Use picture cards instead of written names if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Keep graphing materials organized to prevent slipping or clutter.

items.title: Apple Market
items.objective: Encourage imaginative play while practicing social skills.
items.description: Children pretend to buy and sell apples at a classroom farmers market.
items.materials:
Toy cash register
Toy apples
Grocery baskets
Play money
Shopping bags
items.setup: Create a pretend apple market with baskets of apples and a checkout area.
items.steps:
1. Choose to be a shopper or cashier.
2. Pick apples for your basket.
3. Pretend to pay for the apples.
4. Trade roles with a friend.
5. Practice saying "Thank you" and "You're welcome."
items.teacherRole: Model friendly conversations and encourage sharing and turn-taking.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe communication, cooperation, and role-playing skills.
items.adaptations: Provide visual communication cards for children needing language support.
items.safetyNotes: Use only child-safe dramatic play materials.

items.title: Apple Basket Relay
items.objective: Develop balance and coordination through movement.
items.description: Children carefully carry a pretend apple across the room and place it into a basket before returning to the starting line.
items.materials:
Plastic apples
Small baskets
Music player
Floor markers
items.setup: Place one basket at each end of the activity area.
items.steps:
1. Pick up one apple.
2. Walk carefully to the basket.
3. Place the apple inside.
4. Return to the line.
5. Continue until every apple has been delivered.
items.teacherRole: Encourage careful movement and celebrate teamwork rather than speed.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe balance, body control, and ability to follow directions.
items.adaptations: Reduce the walking distance or allow children to carry lighter objects if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Remind children to walk instead of run and keep pathways clear.

friday.objectives:
Learn that apples grow on trees.
Identify the basic parts of an apple tree.
Sequence the life cycle of an apple from tree to table.
Review apple vocabulary learned throughout the week.
Celebrate everything learned during Apple Week.
friday.materials:
Apple tree poster
Apple life cycle cards
Toy apples
Apple seeds
Flower pictures
Brown and green construction paper
Cotton balls
Glue
Scissors (teacher use or child-safe as appropriate)
Paint
Play dough

Apple books

items.title: Apple Life Cycle
items.objective: Introduce the basic life cycle of an apple.
items.description: Children sequence picture cards showing how apples grow from blossoms into fruit.
items.materials:
Apple life cycle cards
Apple tree poster
Velcro board
items.setup: Arrange the life cycle cards in random order.
items.steps:
1. Look at each picture.
2. Talk about what is happening.
3. Put the pictures in order.
4. Review the sequence together.
5. Repeat as a group.
items.teacherRole: Guide discussion by asking prediction and sequencing questions.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe children's understanding of simple sequencing and plant growth.
items.adaptations: Reduce the sequence to three pictures if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Use large laminated cards appropriate for toddlers.

items.title: Apple Seed Discovery
items.objective: Explore the inside of an apple.
items.description: Children observe an apple cut in half to discover seeds, the core, stem, and flesh while comparing different apples.
items.materials:
Apples
Apple halves
Magnifying glasses
Observation tray
items.setup: Cut apples before the activity and place them on trays.
items.steps:
1. Look inside the apple.
2. Find the seeds.
3. Count the seeds together.
4. Feel the inside of the apple.
5. Compare different apples.
items.teacherRole: Encourage children to ask questions and make observations.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe curiosity, counting skills, and descriptive language.
items.adaptations: Use larger visuals if children have difficulty seeing the seeds.
items.safetyNotes: Closely supervise handling of apple pieces and remind children not to place seeds in their mouths.

items.title: My Apple Tree
items.objective: Create an apple tree while reviewing the week's learning.
items.description: Children build an apple tree using handprints, fingerprints, or paper pieces to represent leaves and apples.
items.materials:
Brown construction paper
Green paint
Red pom-poms or fingerprints
Glue
Paper
items.setup: Prepare tree trunks before children arrive.
items.steps:
1. Glue the tree trunk.
2. Add green leaves.
3. Add red apples.
4. Count the apples on your tree.
5. Share your artwork with the class.
items.teacherRole: Encourage children to explain how apples grow on trees.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe creativity, counting, and vocabulary.
items.adaptations: Provide pre-cut tree pieces or sponge painting if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Use washable, non-toxic materials.

items.title: Apple Harvest Celebration
items.objective: Celebrate the week's learning through music and movement.
items.description: Children pretend to be apple trees growing from tiny seeds before becoming tall trees filled with apples ready to harvest.
items.materials:
Music player
Plastic apples
Baskets
Scarves

items.steps:
1. Curl into a tiny seed.
2. Slowly grow into an apple tree.
3. Stretch your branches high.
4. Pick pretend apples.
5. Fill the baskets while dancing to music.

items.observationOpportunities: Observe coordination, participation, and understanding of the apple life cycle.
items.adaptations: Allow seated movements or teacher assistance when needed.
items.safetyNotes: Maintain open space for movement and remind children to walk while carrying apples.

lessonPlans.title: Apple Orchard Adventure
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: This week, toddlers will explore the exciting world of apple orchards and discover how apples grow from blossoms into fruit before being picked by farmers. Children will learn about apple trees, orchards, harvesting, and the important people who care for fruit trees. Through dramatic play, science investigations, art, music, movement, sensory experiences, and early math activities, children will build a deeper understanding of where apples come from while strengthening communication, fine motor, gross motor, and social-emotional skills.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Understand that apples grow on trees in orchards.
Identify the basic parts of an apple tree.
Learn about farmers and orchard workers.
Explore the apple growing and harvesting process.
Practice counting, sorting, and comparing apples.
Build vocabulary related to orchards and harvesting.
Strengthen fine motor skills through hands-on activities.
Encourage imaginative play by pretending to work in an orchard.
Develop observation skills through nature exploration.
Build confidence working cooperatively with classmates.

items.title: Explore an Apple Tree

Felt tree
Felt apples
Felt leaves
Felt branches
Tree poster

Baskets

3. Pick pretend apples.

items.title: Build an Apple Tree

Green paper leaves
Red paper apples

Construction paper
Crayons

2. Add branches.

4. Add apples.
5. Draw the sky and grass around the tree.

items.title: Growing Apple Trees
items.objective: Strengthen gross motor skills through imaginative movement.
items.description: Children pretend to grow from tiny apple seeds into tall apple trees blowing in the wind before picking ripe apples.
items.setup: Create an open movement space.

1. Curl into a tiny seed.
2. Slowly grow into a tree.
3. Stretch your branches high.
4. Sway like the wind.

items.teacherRole: Lead the movements while reinforcing orchard vocabulary.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe coordination, balance, and participation.
items.adaptations: Allow seated participation or provide teacher assistance as needed.
items.safetyNotes: Ensure plenty of space between children and encourage walking instead of running.

items.title: Apple Blossom Investigation
items.objective: Explore apple blossoms and understand they grow into apples.

Apple blossom photographs
Apple tree poster
Magnifying glasses
Life cycle cards
items.setup: Arrange the pictures on a science table.

1. Look closely at the blossom pictures.
2. Compare blossoms to apples.
3. Find the matching life cycle card.
4. Talk about how blossoms become apples.
5. Review the sequence together.
items.teacherRole: Ask questions that encourage observation and introduce new vocabulary.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe children's curiosity and understanding of the first stage of apple growth.
items.adaptations: Provide larger pictures or one-on-one support if needed.

items.title: Apple Blossom Tree
items.objective: Create an apple tree covered in blossoms.
items.description: Children decorate tree branches with pink tissue paper blossoms and cotton ball clouds to represent springtime in the orchard.
items.materials:
Brown construction paper
Pink tissue paper
Green paper
Cotton balls
Glue
Crayons
items.setup: Prepare tree trunks before children arrive.
items.steps:
1. Glue the tree trunk.
2. Add branches.
3. Crumple pink tissue paper into blossoms.
4. Glue blossoms onto the branches.
5. Add grass and clouds to complete the picture.
items.teacherRole: Discuss how blossoms appear before apples grow.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe hand strength, creativity, and participation.
items.adaptations: Provide pre-cut materials or larger tissue paper pieces.
items.safetyNotes: Use non-toxic glue and supervise all materials.

items.title: Count the Blossoms
items.objective: Develop counting and one-to-one correspondence skills.
items.description: Children count blossom pictures and place the matching number of flowers onto a paper tree.
items.materials:
Blossom cutouts
Number cards 1-5
Paper trees
items.setup: Place blossom cutouts beside each paper tree.
items.steps:
1. Choose a number card.
2. Count the blossoms.
3. Place blossoms on the tree.
4. Count together.
5. Repeat with another number.
items.teacherRole: Model slow counting while encouraging children to touch each blossom.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe counting accuracy and participation.
items.adaptations: Reduce quantities or provide teacher assistance when needed.
items.safetyNotes: Use large blossom pieces appropriate for toddlers.

items.title: Blossoms in the Breeze
items.objective: Strengthen gross motor skills while pretending to be blossoms blowing in the wind.
items.description: Children pretend to be blossoms growing on trees before floating gently to the ground like flower petals.
items.materials:
Music player
Scarves
Artificial flower petals
items.setup: Create a large open movement area.
items.steps:
1. Stand tall like an apple tree.
2. Stretch your branches.
3. Wiggle like blossoms in the breeze.
4. Slowly float to the ground like petals.
5. Stand up and grow into a tree again.
items.teacherRole: Model gentle movements while reinforcing vocabulary.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe balance, coordination, and participation.
items.adaptations: Allow seated movements or teacher assistance if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Maintain clear walking paths and remind children to move carefully.
