items.title: Apple Harvest Crew
items.objective: Encourage cooperative play while pretending to harvest apples.
items.description: Children become orchard workers by picking apples, filling baskets, and delivering them to the harvest station.

Farmer hats
Plastic apples
Baskets
Toy wheelbarrow
items.setup: Place apples throughout the classroom and create a harvest station.
items.steps:
1. Put on a farmer hat.
2. Walk through the orchard.
3. Pick an apple.
4. Place it into your basket.
5. Deliver the basket to the harvest station.
6. Repeat until every apple has been collected.
items.teacherRole: Encourage teamwork and model orchard vocabulary throughout the activity.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe teamwork, communication, and imaginative play.
items.adaptations: Provide lighter baskets or reduce the walking distance if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Remind children to walk while carrying baskets and keep pathways clear.

items.title: Sort the Harvest
items.objective: Practice sorting and counting harvested apples.
items.description: Children sort apples by color and count how many apples were harvested in each basket.
items.materials:
Red, green, and yellow plastic apples
Three sorting baskets
Number cards
items.setup: Mix apples together before beginning.
items.steps:
1. Choose one apple.
2. Identify its color.
3. Place it into the matching basket.
4. Count the apples in each basket.
5. Compare which basket has the most and least apples.
items.teacherRole: Encourage counting, comparing, and color recognition.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe one-to-one correspondence and counting accuracy.
items.adaptations: Begin with only two colors if additional support is needed.
items.safetyNotes: Use only large manipulatives appropriate for toddlers.

items.description: Children decorate a paper basket and fill it with colorful paper apples to represent a successful harvest.

Basket template

Glue sticks
Crayons
Stickers

items.steps:

2. Cut or glue apples into the basket.

items.teacherRole: Encourage children to talk about how farmers collect apples.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe fine motor control and counting skills.
items.adaptations: Provide pre-cut apples or larger materials if needed.

items.title: Harvest Dance
items.objective: Develop coordination while pretending to harvest apples.
items.description: Children dance around the room pretending to climb ladders, reach for apples, carry baskets, and celebrate a successful harvest.

Music player
Plastic apples
Baskets
Scarves
items.setup: Create a large open movement space.
items.steps:
1. Pretend to climb a ladder.
2. Reach up high to pick apples.
3. Carefully carry your basket.
4. Deliver your harvest.
5. Celebrate with a happy harvest dance.
items.teacherRole: Lead movements while reviewing orchard vocabulary.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe coordination, participation, and body awareness.
items.adaptations: Allow seated participation or shorten movement distances when needed.
items.safetyNotes: Keep movement areas free of obstacles and encourage walking instead of running.

Toy cash register
Toy apples
Grocery baskets
Play money
Shopping bags

4. Pretend to pay for the apples.
5. Trade jobs with a friend.
items.teacherRole: Model polite greetings, turn-taking, and simple conversations.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe sharing, role-playing, and language development.

items.title: Apple's Journey
items.objective: Sequence the journey of an apple from tree to table.
items.description: Children place picture cards in order showing how apples travel from the orchard to the grocery store.
items.materials:
Picture sequencing cards
Apple life cycle poster
Velcro board
items.setup: Mix the picture cards before beginning.
items.steps:
1. Look at each picture.
2. Find the farmer.
3. Find the truck.
4. Find the grocery store.
5. Put the pictures in the correct order together.
items.teacherRole: Encourage children to explain each step in the apple's journey.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe sequencing skills and understanding of community helpers.
items.adaptations: Reduce the sequence to three cards if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Use large laminated cards appropriate for toddlers.

items.title: Pack the Apple Boxes
items.objective: Practice counting while packing apples into shipping boxes.
items.description: Children count apples into boxes before they are "delivered" to the grocery store.
items.materials:
Plastic apples
Small boxes
Number cards
items.setup: Place empty boxes beside baskets of apples.
items.steps:
1. Choose a number card.
2. Count the correct number of apples.
3. Pack the apples into the box.
4. Count together.
5. Deliver the box to the pretend truck.
items.teacherRole: Model one-to-one correspondence and encourage counting aloud.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe counting accuracy and confidence.
items.adaptations: Use smaller numbers or teacher support when needed.
items.safetyNotes: Use lightweight boxes and large manipulatives.

items.title: Delivery Driver Adventure
items.objective: Strengthen gross motor skills while pretending to deliver apples.
items.description: Children pretend to drive delivery trucks, stop at traffic signs, unload apple boxes, and deliver fresh apples to the grocery store.
items.materials:
Toy steering wheels
Cones
Apple boxes
Music player
items.setup: Create a pretend road with cones and delivery stations.
items.steps:
1. Pretend to drive your truck.
2. Stop at the stop sign.
3. Drive carefully to the grocery store.
4. Unload the apple boxes.
5. Wave goodbye and drive back for another delivery.
items.teacherRole: Model safe driving, listening skills, and teamwork.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe coordination, listening, and participation.
items.adaptations: Allow children to walk the route instead of pretending to drive if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Maintain clear pathways and remind children to move safely at all times.

items.title: Apple Orchard Parade

items.safetyNotes: Maintain clear walking paths and encourage safe movement throughout the celebration.

lessonPlans.title: Apples in the Kitchen
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: This week, toddlers will discover how apples become delicious foods we enjoy every day. Children will explore washing, cutting, mixing, cooking, tasting, and preparing apples through safe, hands-on experiences. They will learn that apples can be used to make applesauce, apple juice, apple pie, muffins, and other healthy snacks while strengthening early math, science, language, fine motor, and social-emotional skills through engaging kitchen-themed activities.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Discover different foods made from apples.
Practice safe kitchen routines.
Explore healthy eating habits.
Compare raw and cooked apples.
Develop early measuring and counting skills.
Build vocabulary related to cooking and kitchens.
Strengthen fine motor skills through food preparation activities.
Encourage teamwork while preparing pretend recipes.
Explore changes in texture, smell, and taste.
Build confidence trying healthy foods.

items.title: Make Homemade Applesauce
items.objective: Introduce children to preparing a simple healthy snack.
items.description: Children help mash soft cooked apples into applesauce while observing changes in texture and smell.
items.materials:
Soft cooked apples
Potato masher
Mixing bowl
Wooden spoons
Cinnamon (optional)
items.setup: Cook apples before class and allow them to cool to a safe temperature.
items.steps:
1. Look at the cooked apples.
2. Smell the apples.
3. Mash the apples together.
4. Stir the applesauce.
5. Taste a small spoonful if permitted.
items.teacherRole: Discuss each cooking step while encouraging descriptive language about texture, smell, and taste.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe willingness to participate, sensory exploration, and communication.

items.safetyNotes: Check food allergies, supervise tasting closely, and ensure food is served at a safe temperature.

Apple stickers

Crayons
Glue

lessonPlans.title: Johnny Appleseed & Apple Fun
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: This week, toddlers will celebrate Johnny Appleseed while learning how apple trees grow from tiny seeds into large, fruit-bearing trees. Through storytelling, planting, dramatic play, science investigations, sensory exploration, art, music, and movement, children will discover how one person can help nature by planting trees. They will explore apple seeds, life cycles, kindness, caring for plants, and the importance of sharing with others while strengthening early literacy, math, science, fine motor, gross motor, and social-emotional skills.
lessonPlans.objectives:
Learn about Johnny Appleseed in a toddler-friendly way.
Discover that apple trees grow from seeds.
Explore the life cycle of an apple tree.
Practice planting and caring for seeds.
Build vocabulary related to gardening and nature.
Strengthen fine motor skills through planting and art.
Develop early math skills through counting and sorting seeds.
Encourage kindness and helping others.
Build observation skills while caring for plants.
Celebrate everything learned during the Apple unit.

lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Toddlers will learn about the people who help us every day in our homes, schools, and communities. Through dramatic play, books, songs, movement activities, and hands-on exploration, children will discover how helpers such as firefighters, doctors, teachers, farmers, mail carriers, and police officers make our communities safe and strong.

- Develop social awareness and appreciation for helpers

lessonPlans.title: Growing Gardens
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Toddlers will become little gardeners as they explore seeds, plants, flowers, vegetables, insects, and the life cycle of a garden. Through hands-on planting experiences, sensory exploration, art, movement, and observation activities, children will develop curiosity, responsibility, and a deeper understanding of the natural world.

lessonPlans.title: Tummy Time Adventures
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Infants will build strength, coordination, and confidence through developmentally appropriate tummy time experiences. Throughout the week, babies will explore colorful materials, mirrors, sounds, and sensory items that encourage head lifting, visual tracking, reaching, and early exploration while developing important gross motor skills.
lessonPlans.objectives:
- Strengthen neck and shoulder muscles
- Encourage head lifting and visual tracking
- Support reaching and grasping skills
- Promote sensory exploration during tummy time
- Increase tolerance and enjoyment of tummy time experiences
- Build caregiver-child interactions through play

lessonPlans.title: Black & White Discovery

This week babies will explore bold patterns, shapes, and visual experiences designed to strengthen visual focus, tracking, attention, and early brain development. Through play-based activities, infants will observe, reach, listen, and interact with caregivers while building important developmental foundations.

lessonPlans.title: Sensory Discovery
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Infants will explore the world through their senses using hands-on experiences that encourage touching, shaking, squeezing, listening, crawling, and investigating. Throughout the week, children will engage with a variety of textures, sounds, colors, and movement activities that support brain development, curiosity, problem-solving, and sensory processing.
lessonPlans.objectives:
- Encourage sensory exploration through play
- Strengthen fine motor and grasping skills
- Develop problem-solving abilities
- Promote crawling and movement during exploration
- Support language development through sensory vocabulary
- Build curiosity and confidence through discovery

lessonPlans.familyConnection: Encourage families to provide opportunities for safe sensory exploration at home using household textures, sounds, and everyday objects. Talk about what babies are touching, hearing, and experiencing.

lessonPlans.title: Peek-A-Boo & Play
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Infants will participate in playful peek-a-boo experiences that encourage social interaction, visual tracking, language development, and early object permanence skills. Through songs, scarves, mirrors, movement activities, and playful interactions with caregivers, babies will build relationships, confidence, and curiosity while having fun.
lessonPlans.objectives:
- Develop social connections with trusted caregivers
- Strengthen visual tracking skills
- Encourage early object permanence development
- Support language development through repetition
- Promote smiling, laughing, and social engagement
- Encourage reaching and movement during play

lessonPlans.title: Baby's First Conversations
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Communication begins long before babies say their first words. Throughout this week, infants will engage in meaningful back-and-forth interactions through facial expressions, coos, babbles, songs, mirrors, gestures, and responsive caregiving. These experiences help build the foundation for language development, social connection, listening skills, and emotional security.

- Encourage early communication skills
- Support cooing, babbling, and vocal play
- Strengthen caregiver-child interactions
- Develop listening and turn-taking skills
- Promote facial recognition and social engagement
- Build early language foundations

lessonPlans.title: Mirror Me
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Infants are naturally fascinated by faces, expressions, movement, and reflections. Throughout this week, babies will explore mirrors through sensory play, movement, songs, facial expressions, and social interactions. These experiences support self-awareness, visual tracking, communication development, emotional connections, and early cognitive skills while encouraging joyful exploration and discovery.
lessonPlans.objectives:
- Promote self-awareness and identity development
- Encourage visual tracking and attention skills
- Support language development through face-to-face interactions
- Strengthen social-emotional connections
- Encourage reaching, grasping, and movement toward reflections
- Develop curiosity and exploration skills

lessonPlans.title: Peek-A-Boo Fun
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Peek-a-boo is more than a game—it helps infants develop object permanence, social connections, communication skills, memory, anticipation, and emotional security. Throughout the week, infants will participate in playful peek-a-boo experiences using scarves, mirrors, puppets, tunnels, boxes, and movement activities designed to strengthen early learning through joyful interactions.
lessonPlans.objectives:
- Develop object permanence skills
- Encourage social interaction and communication
- Strengthen visual tracking abilities
- Promote anticipation and memory development
- Support emotional security through predictable play
- Encourage movement, reaching, and exploration

lessonPlans.title: Construction Engineers
lessonPlans.weeklyOverview: Children will become construction engineers as they design buildings, test structures, operate construction sites, explore tools, and solve engineering challenges. Through hands-on building experiences and STEM investigations, children will develop creativity, problem-solving, and teamwork skills.
lessonPlans.objectives:
• Explore engineering and construction concepts
• Practice planning and problem-solving
• Develop measurement and building skills
• Strengthen teamwork and communication
• Build fine and gross motor abilities
lessonPlans.weeklyMaterials: Blocks, measuring tapes, toy tools, hard hats, cardboard boxes, blueprints, rulers, clipboards, construction vehicles
lessonPlans.vocabularyWords: Engineer, Builder, Blueprint, Structure, Measure, Construct, Tool, Foundation, Design, Build
lessonPlans.observationOpportunities: Observe problem-solving, teamwork, measuring skills, communication, and creativity during building activities.
lessonPlans.adaptations: Provide larger building materials, visual supports, adaptive tools, peer partnerships, and additional teacher support.
lessonPlans.familyConnection: Encourage families to identify construction projects in the community and discuss how buildings are made.

activities.title: Pom-Pom Color Sort
activities.objective: Practice matching and sorting colors using fine motor skills.
activities.description: Preschoolers sort pom-poms into matching colored cups or bowls.
activities.materials: Colored cups or bowls, pom-poms in assorted colors, tweezers (optional)
activities.setup: Arrange colored cups on a table with a bowl of mixed pom-poms.
activities.steps:
1. Introduce the colored cups and name each color.
2. Demonstrate sorting one pom-pom into the matching cup.

activities.description: Toddlers explore Pet Sensory Exploration during our Pet Vet Clinic week through sensory play.
activities.materials:
sensory bin materials
Sensory bin
Scoops
Loose parts
activities.setup: Prepare a toddler-ready space and materials for Pet Sensory Exploration.
activities.steps:
1. Set out a toddler-safe sensory experience for Pet Sensory Exploration.
2. Model gentle scooping, pouring, and exploring with fingers or tools.
3. Name textures, colors, and theme vocabulary as children play.
4. Rotate materials if interest fades and keep play short and calm.
activities.teacherRole: Supervise closely, model gentle exploration, and support sensory preferences.
learningGoals: Engage in Pet Sensory Exploration through toddler-friendly sensory play.
Use theme vocabulary related to Pet Vet Clinic.
Practice social interaction, curiosity, and motor skills during play.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe engagement, theme vocabulary, motor skills, and social interaction.
activities.adaptations: Offer larger materials, hand-over-hand support, and a shorter turn. Allow parallel play instead of forced sharing.
activities.safetyNotes: Supervise closely, keep materials too large to choke on, and clear walkways for active movement. Check outdoor surfaces before play.
