activities.objective: Recognize each child's contributions to the classroom community.
activities.description: Each child receives a Classroom Helper certificate while classmates clap and celebrate one another's efforts throughout the week.
activities.setup: Arrange children in a circle.
activities.steps:
1. Call each child by name.
2. Present their Classroom Helper certificate.
3. Share one positive helper job they completed.
4. Encourage classmates to clap and cheer.
5. End with a group celebration photo if permission has been provided.
activities.teacherRole: Celebrate every child's growth and encourage continued responsibility.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe confidence, peer support, and emotional responses.
activities.adaptations: Present certificates individually for children who prefer less attention.
activities.safetyNotes: Ensure children remain seated while waiting for their turn.

activities.title: Mirror, Mirror, Happy Me
activities.objective: Help children recognize and identify happy facial expressions.
activities.description: Children explore their own facial expressions using handheld mirrors while practicing smiling and identifying happy emotions.
activities.setup: Place mirrors in a circle with emotion cards nearby.
activities.steps:
1. Show the happy emotion card.
2. Ask children to copy the happy face.
3. Look in the mirrors together.
4. Talk about when they feel happy.
5. Celebrate everyone's beautiful smiles.
activities.teacherRole: Model positive facial expressions and encourage conversation about emotions.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to imitate facial expressions and describe happy feelings.
activities.adaptations: Use teacher modeling or peer modeling for children needing additional support.
activities.safetyNotes: Use child-safe mirrors and supervise appropriately.

activities.title: Happy Face Craft
activities.objective: Encourage children to express happiness creatively.
activities.description: Children create their own smiling face using paper, crayons, stickers, and yarn.
activities.materials:
Happy face templates
Crayons
Stickers
Glue
Yarn
activities.setup: Prepare craft materials at tables.
activities.steps:
1. Give each child a face template.
2. Draw happy eyes and a smile.
3. Decorate with stickers.
4. Add yarn for hair.
5. Display everyone's happy faces on a bulletin board.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe creativity, participation, and conversations about feelings.
activities.adaptations: Provide pre-cut pieces or adaptive crayons if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Closely supervise glue and small craft materials.

activities.title: Happy Dance Party
activities.objective: Express happiness through music and movement.
activities.description: Children dance, jump, clap, and move to upbeat music while practicing happy expressions.
activities.setup: Clear an open space for dancing.
activities.steps:
1. Play upbeat music.
2. Dance with scarves.
3. Smile at classmates.
4. Freeze when the music stops.
5. Share something that makes you happy.
activities.teacherRole: Model joyful movement and encourage participation.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe participation, coordination, and emotional expression.
activities.adaptations: Allow seated dancing or simplified movements if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Maintain safe spacing between children during movement.

activities.title: Happy Puppets
activities.objective: Practice talking about happy feelings.
activities.description: Children use puppets to act out happy classroom situations such as making a friend, sharing toys, or reading together.
activities.setup: Create a small puppet theater area.
activities.steps:
1. Introduce the puppets.
2. Show a happy emotion card.
3. Invite children to make the puppet feel happy.
4. Act out simple classroom scenarios.
5. Discuss what made each puppet happy.
activities.teacherRole: Guide conversations and model emotion vocabulary.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's language, empathy, and imaginative play.
activities.adaptations: Offer sentence starters or model responses for children needing support.
activities.safetyNotes: Use soft puppets without removable small parts.

activities.title: Feelings Mirror
activities.objective: Help children recognize sad facial expressions.
activities.description: Children use mirrors to practice making sad faces and discuss times they have felt sad.
activities.setup: Sit together in a circle with mirrors.
activities.steps:
1. Show the sad emotion card.
2. Make a sad face together.
3. Look in mirrors.
4. Talk about a time they felt sad.
5. Discuss who can help when we're sad.
activities.teacherRole: Provide reassurance and encourage children to share only if they feel comfortable.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to recognize and describe sadness.
activities.adaptations: Allow children to point to emotion cards instead of speaking.
activities.safetyNotes: Use child-safe mirrors and supervise closely.

activities.title: Rainy Day Feelings Cloud
activities.objective: Express emotions through art.
activities.description: Children create a cloud with blue raindrops representing feelings, then decorate it with a rainbow to remind them that happy feelings return.
activities.materials:
Blue construction paper
Cotton balls
Glue
Crayons
Markers
activities.setup: Prepare cloud templates before the activity.
activities.steps:
1. Glue cotton balls onto the cloud.
2. Add blue raindrops.
3. Draw a rainbow underneath.
4. Talk about what helps us feel better.
5. Display the artwork.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage conversations about healthy emotional expression.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe participation and emotional understanding.
activities.adaptations: Offer pre-cut pieces or adaptive art tools.
activities.safetyNotes: Closely supervise glue use.

activities.title: Helping a Friend
activities.objective: Develop empathy and kindness.
activities.description: Children use stuffed animals and puppets to comfort a friend who feels sad.
activities.setup: Create a cozy dramatic play area.
activities.steps:
1. Introduce a puppet who feels sad.
2. Ask children how they can help.
3. Practice giving hugs (if appropriate), kind words, or blankets.
4. Take turns helping the puppet.
5. Celebrate acts of kindness.
activities.teacherRole: Model empathy and respectful caring behaviors.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's caring behaviors and interactions.
activities.adaptations: Model responses for children needing support.
activities.safetyNotes: Respect children's personal boundaries and encourage asking before giving hugs.

activities.title: Calm Breathing with Feathers
activities.objective: Introduce a simple calming strategy.
activities.description: Children practice slow breathing while gently blowing lightweight feathers into the air.
activities.setup: Have children sit comfortably in a circle.
activities.steps:
1. Show how to take a deep breath.
2. Blow gently on a feather.
3. Watch it float.
4. Repeat several slow breaths.
5. Shake the calm-down bottle and quietly observe it settle.
activities.teacherRole: Model slow breathing and calm behavior.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to participate in calming exercises.
activities.adaptations: Use bubbles instead of feathers for children who find blowing easier.
activities.safetyNotes: Closely supervise feathers and remind children not to put them in their mouths.

activities.title: Mad or Calm?
activities.objective: Help children recognize the difference between angry and calm emotions.
activities.description: Children look at emotion cards and decide whether each person feels mad or calm, then practice making both facial expressions.
activities.setup: Place emotion cards in the center of the circle.
activities.steps:
1. Show an emotion card.
2. Ask children how the person feels.
3. Make the same face in the mirror.
4. Talk about what helps us calm down.
5. Practice taking one deep breath together.
activities.teacherRole: Model calm responses and encourage children to name emotions.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to recognize anger and discuss calming strategies.
activities.adaptations: Allow children to point to emotion cards if they are not ready to verbalize responses.
activities.safetyNotes: Use child-safe mirrors and supervise throughout the activity.

activities.title: Tear and Glue Feelings Heart
activities.objective: Express emotions through a calming art activity.
activities.description: Children tear red tissue paper into small pieces and glue them onto a heart while talking about healthy ways to calm down when upset.
activities.materials:
Heart templates
Red tissue paper
Glue sticks
Crayons
activities.setup: Prepare heart templates before the activity.
activities.steps:
1. Give each child a heart template.
2. Tear tissue paper into small pieces.
3. Glue pieces onto the heart.
4. Decorate with crayons.
5. Share one thing that helps you feel calm.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage emotional conversations while assisting with fine motor skills.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe participation and ability to discuss calming ideas.
activities.adaptations: Offer pre-cut paper or larger pieces if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Closely supervise glue and art materials.

activities.title: Pinwheel Breathing
activities.objective: Teach deep breathing as a calming strategy.
activities.description: Children practice slow, controlled breathing by blowing pinwheels.
activities.setup: Seat children comfortably in a circle.
activities.steps:
1. Hold the pinwheel.
2. Take a slow deep breath.
3. Blow gently to make it spin.
4. Repeat several times.
5. Watch the calm-down bottle settle.
activities.teacherRole: Model slow breathing and praise children's efforts.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to participate in calming exercises.
activities.adaptations: Use bubbles instead of pinwheels if preferred.
activities.safetyNotes: Remind children not to place pinwheels in their mouths.

activities.title: Helping the Mad Monster
activities.objective: Practice problem-solving and empathy.
activities.description: A puppet feels angry because something didn't go its way. Children suggest safe ways to help the puppet calm down.
activities.materials:
Monster puppet
Stuffed animals
Emotion cards
activities.setup: Create a small puppet stage.
activities.steps:
1. Introduce the angry puppet.
2. Ask what happened.
3. Brainstorm ways to help.
4. Practice deep breathing with the puppet.
5. Celebrate when the puppet feels calm.
activities.teacherRole: Guide children toward healthy coping strategies and respectful communication.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to suggest calming strategies and show empathy.
activities.adaptations: Offer visual calming cards or sentence starters.
activities.safetyNotes: Use soft puppets and supervise dramatic play.

activities.title: Brave Faces
activities.objective: Help children recognize and talk about feeling scared.
activities.description: Children use mirrors to make scared and brave faces while discussing situations that might make someone nervous.
activities.setup: Sit together in a circle.
activities.steps:
1. Show the scared emotion card.
2. Make a scared face together.
3. Look in the mirrors.
4. Practice changing the scared face into a brave smile.
5. Talk about who helps us feel safe.
activities.teacherRole: Provide reassurance and encourage children to share experiences if they feel comfortable.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to recognize fear and identify trusted adults.
activities.adaptations: Allow children to point to emotion cards instead of speaking.
activities.safetyNotes: Use child-safe mirrors and supervise appropriately.

activities.title: Helping Teddy Feel Brave
activities.objective: Develop empathy and problem-solving skills.
activities.description: Children comfort a teddy bear that feels scared and suggest ways to help it feel safe.
activities.setup: Create a cozy comfort corner.
activities.steps:
1. Introduce Teddy, who feels scared.
2. Ask children how they can help.
3. Wrap Teddy in a blanket or give a gentle pat.
4. Practice saying kind words like, "You're safe."
5. Celebrate helping Teddy feel brave.
activities.teacherRole: Model empathy, kindness, and reassuring language.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe caring behaviors and emotional understanding.
activities.adaptations: Model responses or offer visual choices for children needing support.
activities.safetyNotes: Respect children's personal space and encourage asking permission before hugs.

activities.title: Brave Adventure Course
activities.objective: Build confidence while trying new challenges.
activities.description: Children complete a simple obstacle course while teachers and classmates cheer them on.
activities.materials:
Tunnels
Floor spots
Cones
Balance beam or tape line
activities.setup: Create a safe obstacle course with plenty of space.
activities.steps:
1. Demonstrate each obstacle.
2. Encourage children to try one step at a time.
3. Cheer for each classmate.
4. Celebrate every accomplishment.
5. Talk about how trying something new can make us feel brave.
activities.teacherRole: Provide encouragement and assist children when needed.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe willingness to try new activities and ask for help.
activities.adaptations: Modify obstacles based on each child's ability.
activities.safetyNotes: Closely supervise all climbing and balancing activities.

activities.title: My Brave Star
activities.objective: Celebrate courage and confidence.
activities.description: Children decorate a large star representing something brave they did today.
activities.setup: Prepare star templates before the activity.
activities.steps:
1. Give each child a star.
2. Decorate with crayons and stickers.
3. Talk about one brave thing they did today.
4. Write each child's words on the star.
5. Display the stars on a "Brave at School" bulletin board.
activities.teacherRole: Celebrate every child's effort and encourage positive self-talk.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe participation and confidence while sharing.
activities.adaptations: Offer adaptive art tools or teacher assistance as needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Use only child-safe art supplies.

activities.title: Feelings Match-Up
activities.objective: Review and identify multiple emotions.
activities.description: Children match emotion cards to the correct facial expressions and talk about situations when someone might feel each emotion.
activities.setup: Spread emotion cards on the floor in a circle.
activities.steps:
1. Show an emotion card.
2. Ask children to name the feeling.
3. Match the card to the Feelings Chart.
4. Make the matching facial expression.
5. Talk about one time someone might feel that emotion.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage discussion and reinforce that every feeling is okay.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to identify and describe emotions.
activities.adaptations: Provide visual choices or simplify to two emotions at a time if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Ensure cards remain clean and free from slipping hazards.

activities.title: My Feelings Wheel
activities.objective: Create a visual reminder of different emotions.
activities.description: Children decorate a feelings wheel showing happy, sad, mad, scared, and calm faces.
activities.materials:
Feelings wheel template
Crayons
Markers
Stickers
Paper fastener (teacher assembly)
activities.setup: Prepare wheel templates before the activity.
activities.steps:
1. Color each emotion.
2. Talk about each feeling.
3. Assemble the wheel with teacher assistance.
4. Spin the wheel and name the feeling.
5. Take the wheel home to share with family.
activities.teacherRole: Support children while encouraging conversations about emotions.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe understanding of different emotions and participation.
activities.adaptations: Provide pre-colored examples or adaptive crayons as needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Teacher should assemble wheels using paper fasteners.

activities.title: Feelings Freeze Dance
activities.objective: Express emotions through movement.
activities.description: Children dance while music plays. When the music stops, the teacher holds up an emotion card and children freeze showing that feeling with their face and body.
activities.setup: Clear a large open movement area.
activities.steps:
1. Dance while music plays.
2. Freeze when the music stops.
3. Show the emotion on the card.
4. Talk briefly about the feeling.
5. Repeat using different emotions.
activities.teacherRole: Model facial expressions and encourage participation.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe emotional recognition and body control.
activities.adaptations: Allow seated participation or simplified movements.
activities.safetyNotes: Maintain safe spacing between children during movement.

activities.title: Feelings Superstar Celebration
activities.objective: Celebrate each child's emotional growth throughout the week.
activities.description: Children receive recognition for learning about feelings and practicing kindness, bravery, and healthy emotional expression.
activities.setup: Arrange children in a circle.
activities.steps:
1. Review the week's emotions.
2. Call each child by name.
3. Share one positive thing the child practiced this week.
4. Present a certificate or sticker.
5. End with a class cheer and group photo if permission has been provided.
activities.teacherRole: Celebrate every child's growth while building confidence and belonging.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe confidence, peer encouragement, and participation.
activities.adaptations: Present recognition individually for children who prefer less attention.
activities.safetyNotes: Ensure children remain seated while waiting for their turn.

activities.title: Apple Investigation
activities.objective: Introduce children to observing apples using their five senses.
activities.description: Children investigate real apples by looking, touching, smelling, and listening while learning descriptive vocabulary.
activities.materials:
Red, green, and yellow apples
Magnifying glasses
activities.setup: Place apples in the center of the table with magnifying glasses nearby.
activities.steps:
1. Give each child an apple.
2. Look closely using magnifying glasses.
3. Feel the smooth skin.
4. Smell the apple.
5. Tap gently and listen to the sound.
6. Talk about what everyone noticed.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage observation by asking open-ended questions and introducing new vocabulary.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's willingness to explore and describe the apples.
activities.adaptations: Provide larger apples or additional teacher support as needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Closely supervise children while handling real apples.

activities.title: Apple Stamp Painting
activities.objective: Explore color while creating apple artwork.
activities.description: Children use apple halves dipped in paint to create colorful apple prints.
activities.materials:
Apple halves
Red, green, and yellow paint
White construction paper
Smocks
activities.setup: Cut apples in half before the activity and pour paint into shallow trays.
activities.steps:
1. Dip the apple into paint.
2. Press onto paper.
3. Lift carefully.
4. Repeat using different colors.
5. Allow artwork to dry for display.
activities.teacherRole: Model stamping techniques and encourage color recognition.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe hand control and participation.
activities.adaptations: Provide sponge stamps if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Use only non-toxic washable paint and supervise closely.

activities.title: Count the Apples
activities.objective: Practice one-to-one counting.
activities.description: Children count plastic apples and place them into baskets.
activities.materials:
Plastic apples
Small baskets
Number cards 1–5
activities.setup: Place apples beside empty baskets.
activities.steps:
1. Choose a number card.
2. Count the correct number of apples.
3. Place apples into the basket.
4. Count together.
5. Repeat with another number.
activities.teacherRole: Model counting slowly and encourage children to touch each apple as they count.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe counting accuracy and participation.
activities.adaptations: Reduce the number of apples or provide hand-over-hand assistance.
activities.safetyNotes: Use large manipulatives to prevent choking hazards.

activities.title: Pick the Apples
activities.objective: Develop gross motor skills while reinforcing apple vocabulary.
activities.description: Children pretend to reach high into an apple tree, pick apples, place them in baskets, and carry them to the pretend orchard.
activities.materials:
Music player
Apple baskets
Plastic apples
activities.setup: Scatter plastic apples around the classroom.
activities.steps:
1. Play apple-themed music.
2. Pretend to reach high into the tree.
3. Pick an apple.
4. Carry it to the basket.
5. Repeat until all apples have been collected.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage movement, counting, and imaginative play.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe balance, coordination, and participation.
activities.adaptations: Place apples within easy reach or allow seated participation if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Ensure children walk while carrying apples and keep the activity area free of obstacles.

activities.title: Apple Color Sort
activities.objective: Develop color recognition and sorting skills.
activities.description: Children sort apples into matching colored baskets while practicing color vocabulary.
activities.materials:
Plastic apples
Red basket
Green basket
Yellow basket
activities.setup: Mix all apples together in one large basket.
activities.steps:
1. Show each colored basket.
2. Pick up one apple.
3. Name its color.
4. Place it into the matching basket.
5. Count how many apples are in each basket.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage children to say each color aloud while sorting.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to identify and sort colors correctly.
activities.adaptations: Use only two colors if children need a simpler activity.
activities.safetyNotes: Use large manipulatives appropriate for toddlers.

activities.title: My Favorite Apple Color
activities.objective: Explore colors through creative expression.
activities.description: Children create a colorful apple collage using tissue paper, paint, and stickers.
activities.materials:
Apple templates
Red, green, and yellow tissue paper
Glue sticks
Stickers
Crayons
activities.setup: Prepare apple templates before the activity.
activities.steps:
1. Choose a favorite apple color.
2. Glue tissue paper onto the apple.
3. Decorate with crayons and stickers.
4. Share your favorite apple color.
5. Display artwork around the classroom.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage creativity while reinforcing color names.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe color choices and participation.
activities.adaptations: Offer larger tissue paper pieces or sponge painting.
activities.safetyNotes: Closely supervise glue and art materials.

activities.title: Apple Color Investigation
activities.objective: Compare apples by observing their colors and features.
activities.description: Children closely examine apples to discover that apples can be different colors while still being the same fruit.
activities.setup: Arrange apples on a science table.
activities.steps:
1. Observe each apple.
2. Compare the colors.
3. Feel the apples.
4. Talk about what is the same and different.
5. Decide which apple is your favorite.
activities.teacherRole: Ask open-ended questions and encourage careful observation.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe curiosity and descriptive language.
activities.adaptations: Allow children to work with a partner.
activities.safetyNotes: Inspect apples before handling.

activities.title: Apple Color Dance
activities.objective: Reinforce color recognition through movement.
activities.description: Children dance while holding colorful scarves. When the music stops, the teacher calls a color and children find the matching apple.
activities.materials:
Music player
Color scarves
Plastic apples
activities.setup: Scatter apples throughout the room.
activities.steps:
1. Dance with scarves.
2. Freeze when the music stops.
3. Listen for a color.
4. Find the matching apple.
5. Repeat with different colors.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage movement and celebrate successful color matching.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe listening, coordination, and color identification.
activities.adaptations: Reduce the number of colors or provide teacher guidance.
activities.safetyNotes: Keep the movement area clear and remind children to walk while finding apples.

activities.title: Big or Small?
activities.objective: Develop comparison and classification skills.
activities.description: Children compare apples by size and sort them into "Big" and "Small" baskets.
activities.materials:
Large apples
Small apples
Two baskets
Size labels
activities.setup: Mix apples together in one large basket.
activities.steps:
1. Show the two baskets.
2. Pick up one apple.
3. Decide if it is big or small.
4. Place it into the correct basket.
5. Count the apples in each basket.
activities.teacherRole: Model comparison words and encourage children to explain their thinking.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to compare sizes and classify objects.
activities.adaptations: Begin with only two noticeably different sizes before introducing medium apples.
activities.safetyNotes: Use age-appropriate apples and supervise closely.

activities.title: Apple Measuring Station
activities.objective: Introduce simple measurement concepts.
activities.description: Children explore how apples can be measured using yarn, measuring tape, or linking cubes.
activities.materials:
Apples
Measuring tape
Yarn
Linking cubes
activities.setup: Arrange measuring materials on a science table.
activities.steps:
1. Choose an apple.
2. Wrap yarn around the apple.
3. Compare the yarn lengths.
4. Count linking cubes if using them.
5. Talk about which apple is bigger.
activities.teacherRole: Introduce simple measurement vocabulary while encouraging exploration.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe curiosity and understanding of measurement.
activities.adaptations: Use only one measuring tool if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Closely supervise measuring materials.

activities.title: Round Apple Collage
activities.objective: Recognize the round shape of an apple.
activities.description: Children create a collage using paper circles to build colorful apples.
activities.materials:
Red, green, and yellow paper circles
Glue sticks
Construction paper
Crayons
Brown and green paper strips
activities.setup: Prepare paper circles and stems before the activity.
activities.steps:
1. Choose a paper circle.
2. Glue it onto the paper.
3. Add a stem and leaf.
4. Decorate the background.
5. Share your apple with the class.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe shape recognition and fine motor skills.
activities.adaptations: Offer larger paper pieces or pre-glued examples.
activities.safetyNotes: Use child-safe scissors only if needed with close supervision.

activities.title: Roll Like an Apple
activities.objective: Develop body awareness and gross motor skills.
activities.description: Children pretend to be apples by curling into a ball, rolling carefully on mats, stretching into apple trees, and reaching high to pick pretend apples.
activities.materials:
Gym mats
Music player
Bean bags
activities.setup: Create a large open movement area with mats.
activities.steps:
1. Pretend to grow into an apple tree.
2. Reach up high.
3. Curl into a round apple.
4. Carefully roll across the mat.
5. Stand up and pretend to place your apple into a basket.
activities.teacherRole: Model each movement and encourage safe participation.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe balance, coordination, and participation.
activities.adaptations: Allow children to perform movements while seated or with teacher assistance.
activities.safetyNotes: Use mats on a flat surface and supervise rolling activities closely.

activities.title: Apple Taste Test
activities.objective: Explore different apple varieties using the sense of taste.
activities.description: Children sample small pieces of red, green, and yellow apples while comparing their flavors and textures.
activities.materials:
Red apples
Green apples
Yellow apples
Small plates
Napkins
activities.setup: Wash and slice apples before children arrive. Place one slice of each apple on every plate.
activities.steps:
1. Look at each apple.
2. Smell each apple.
3. Taste one slice at a time.
4. Talk about which apple tastes sweet, tart, or crunchy.
5. Choose your favorite apple.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage children to describe what they taste while respecting that everyone may have different preferences.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's willingness to try new foods and describe their experiences.
activities.adaptations: Offer only one apple variety if children are hesitant or have sensory sensitivities.
activities.safetyNotes: Always check for food allergies. Cut apples into small bite-sized pieces and supervise closely during tasting.

activities.title: Favorite Apple Graph
activities.objective: Introduce simple graphing and counting skills.
activities.description: Children place their name or sticker above their favorite apple color to create a classroom graph.
activities.materials:
Large graph paper
Apple color pictures
Name cards or stickers
activities.setup: Prepare a graph with three columns labeled Red, Green, and Yellow.
activities.steps:
1. Decide your favorite apple.
2. Find the matching column.
3. Place your sticker.
4. Count each column together.
5. Discover which apple was the class favorite.
activities.teacherRole: Guide children through counting and comparing which column has the most and least.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe counting skills and ability to interpret simple graphs.
activities.adaptations: Use picture cards instead of written names if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Keep graphing materials organized to prevent slipping or clutter.

activities.title: Apple Market
activities.objective: Encourage imaginative play while practicing social skills.
activities.description: Children pretend to buy and sell apples at a classroom farmers market.
activities.materials:
Toy cash register
Toy apples
Grocery baskets
Play money
Shopping bags
activities.setup: Create a pretend apple market with baskets of apples and a checkout area.
activities.steps:
1. Choose to be a shopper or cashier.
2. Pick apples for your basket.
3. Pretend to pay for the apples.
4. Trade roles with a friend.
5. Practice saying "Thank you" and "You're welcome."
activities.teacherRole: Model friendly conversations and encourage sharing and turn-taking.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe communication, cooperation, and role-playing skills.
activities.adaptations: Provide visual communication cards for children needing language support.
activities.safetyNotes: Use only child-safe dramatic play materials.

activities.title: Apple Basket Relay
activities.objective: Develop balance and coordination through movement.
activities.description: Children carefully carry a pretend apple across the room and place it into a basket before returning to the starting line.
activities.materials:
Plastic apples
Small baskets
Music player
Floor markers
activities.setup: Place one basket at each end of the activity area.
activities.steps:
1. Pick up one apple.
2. Walk carefully to the basket.
3. Place the apple inside.
4. Return to the line.
5. Continue until every apple has been delivered.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage careful movement and celebrate teamwork rather than speed.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe balance, body control, and ability to follow directions.
activities.adaptations: Reduce the walking distance or allow children to carry lighter objects if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Remind children to walk instead of run and keep pathways clear.

activities.title: Apple Life Cycle
activities.objective: Introduce the basic life cycle of an apple.
activities.description: Children sequence picture cards showing how apples grow from blossoms into fruit.
activities.materials:
Apple life cycle cards
Apple tree poster
Velcro board
activities.setup: Arrange the life cycle cards in random order.
activities.steps:
1. Look at each picture.
2. Talk about what is happening.
3. Put the pictures in order.
4. Review the sequence together.
5. Repeat as a group.
activities.teacherRole: Guide discussion by asking prediction and sequencing questions.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's understanding of simple sequencing and plant growth.
activities.adaptations: Reduce the sequence to three pictures if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Use large laminated cards appropriate for toddlers.

activities.title: Apple Seed Discovery
activities.objective: Explore the inside of an apple.
activities.description: Children observe an apple cut in half to discover seeds, the core, stem, and flesh while comparing different apples.
activities.materials:
Apples
Apple halves
Magnifying glasses
Observation tray
activities.setup: Cut apples before the activity and place them on trays.
activities.steps:
1. Look inside the apple.
2. Find the seeds.
3. Count the seeds together.
4. Feel the inside of the apple.
5. Compare different apples.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage children to ask questions and make observations.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe curiosity, counting skills, and descriptive language.
activities.adaptations: Use larger visuals if children have difficulty seeing the seeds.
activities.safetyNotes: Closely supervise handling of apple pieces and remind children not to place seeds in their mouths.

activities.title: My Apple Tree
activities.objective: Create an apple tree while reviewing the week's learning.
activities.description: Children build an apple tree using handprints, fingerprints, or paper pieces to represent leaves and apples.
activities.materials:
Brown construction paper
Green paint
Red pom-poms or fingerprints
Glue
Paper
activities.setup: Prepare tree trunks before children arrive.
activities.steps:
1. Glue the tree trunk.
2. Add green leaves.
3. Add red apples.
4. Count the apples on your tree.
5. Share your artwork with the class.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage children to explain how apples grow on trees.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe creativity, counting, and vocabulary.
activities.adaptations: Provide pre-cut tree pieces or sponge painting if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Use washable, non-toxic materials.

activities.title: Apple Harvest Celebration
activities.objective: Celebrate the week's learning through music and movement.
activities.description: Children pretend to be apple trees growing from tiny seeds before becoming tall trees filled with apples ready to harvest.
activities.materials:
Music player
Plastic apples
Baskets
Scarves
activities.setup: Scatter apples around the room and provide baskets.
activities.steps:
1. Curl into a tiny seed.
2. Slowly grow into an apple tree.
3. Stretch your branches high.
4. Pick pretend apples.
5. Fill the baskets while dancing to music.
activities.teacherRole: Lead movement while reviewing everything learned about apples.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe coordination, participation, and understanding of the apple life cycle.
activities.adaptations: Allow seated movements or teacher assistance when needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Maintain open space for movement and remind children to walk while carrying apples.

activities.title: Explore an Apple Tree
activities.objective: Identify the main parts of an apple tree.
activities.description: Children observe an apple tree poster and match felt pieces to build their own apple tree.
activities.materials:
Felt tree
Felt apples
Felt leaves
Felt branches
Tree poster
activities.setup: Place the felt tree on a flannel board with all pieces nearby.
activities.steps:
1. Look at the apple tree poster.
2. Find the tree trunk.
3. Add branches and leaves.
4. Place apples on the branches.
5. Name each part together.
activities.teacherRole: Model tree vocabulary and encourage children to point to each part as they name it.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to identify and name tree parts.
activities.adaptations: Provide larger felt pieces or individual boards as needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Keep felt pieces large enough to prevent choking hazards.

activities.title: Little Apple Farmers
activities.objective: Encourage imaginative play while learning about orchard workers.
activities.description: Children pretend to be farmers picking apples and placing them into baskets for customers.
activities.materials:
Farmer hats
Toy apples
Baskets
Play crates
activities.setup: Create a pretend orchard with baskets placed around the room.
activities.steps:
1. Put on a farmer hat.
2. Walk through the orchard.
3. Pick pretend apples.
4. Place apples into baskets.
5. Deliver the baskets to the pretend market.
activities.teacherRole: Model farm vocabulary and encourage teamwork.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe sharing, communication, and role-playing.
activities.adaptations: Provide picture cue cards for children needing language support.
activities.safetyNotes: Encourage walking feet while carrying baskets.

activities.title: Build an Apple Tree
activities.objective: Create an apple tree using different art materials.
activities.description: Children glue together a tree trunk, branches, leaves, and apples to make their own orchard tree.
activities.materials:
Brown paper trunks
Green paper leaves
Red paper apples
Glue
Construction paper
Crayons
activities.setup: Prepare all tree pieces before the activity.
activities.steps:
1. Glue the tree trunk.
2. Add branches.
3. Glue on leaves.
4. Add apples.
5. Draw the sky and grass around the tree.
activities.teacherRole: Discuss each tree part while children work.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe cutting, gluing, and naming tree parts.
activities.adaptations: Offer preassembled pieces or larger materials if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Use child-safe glue and supervise all materials.

activities.title: Growing Apple Trees
activities.objective: Strengthen gross motor skills through imaginative movement.
activities.description: Children pretend to grow from tiny apple seeds into tall apple trees blowing in the wind before picking ripe apples.
activities.setup: Create an open movement space.
activities.steps:
1. Curl into a tiny seed.
2. Slowly grow into a tree.
3. Stretch your branches high.
4. Sway like the wind.
5. Reach up and pick pretend apples.
activities.teacherRole: Lead the movements while reinforcing orchard vocabulary.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe coordination, balance, and participation.
activities.adaptations: Allow seated participation or provide teacher assistance as needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Ensure plenty of space between children and encourage walking instead of running.

activities.title: Apple Blossom Investigation
activities.objective: Explore apple blossoms and understand they grow into apples.
activities.description: Children examine blossom pictures and compare them to apples while learning the first stage of the apple life cycle.
activities.materials:
Apple blossom photographs
Apple tree poster
Magnifying glasses
Life cycle cards
activities.setup: Arrange the pictures on a science table.
activities.steps:
1. Look closely at the blossom pictures.
2. Compare blossoms to apples.
3. Find the matching life cycle card.
4. Talk about how blossoms become apples.
5. Review the sequence together.
activities.teacherRole: Ask questions that encourage observation and introduce new vocabulary.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's curiosity and understanding of the first stage of apple growth.
activities.adaptations: Provide larger pictures or one-on-one support if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Remind children to handle photographs and materials gently.

activities.title: Apple Blossom Tree
activities.objective: Create an apple tree covered in blossoms.
activities.description: Children decorate tree branches with pink tissue paper blossoms and cotton ball clouds to represent springtime in the orchard.
activities.materials:
Brown construction paper
Pink tissue paper
Green paper
Cotton balls
Glue
Crayons
activities.setup: Prepare tree trunks before children arrive.
activities.steps:
1. Glue the tree trunk.
2. Add branches.
3. Crumple pink tissue paper into blossoms.
4. Glue blossoms onto the branches.
5. Add grass and clouds to complete the picture.
activities.teacherRole: Discuss how blossoms appear before apples grow.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe hand strength, creativity, and participation.
activities.adaptations: Provide pre-cut materials or larger tissue paper pieces.
activities.safetyNotes: Use non-toxic glue and supervise all materials.

activities.title: Count the Blossoms
activities.objective: Develop counting and one-to-one correspondence skills.
activities.description: Children count blossom pictures and place the matching number of flowers onto a paper tree.
activities.materials:
Blossom cutouts
Number cards 1-5
Paper trees
activities.setup: Place blossom cutouts beside each paper tree.
activities.steps:
1. Choose a number card.
2. Count the blossoms.
3. Place blossoms on the tree.
4. Count together.
5. Repeat with another number.
activities.teacherRole: Model slow counting while encouraging children to touch each blossom.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe counting accuracy and participation.
activities.adaptations: Reduce quantities or provide teacher assistance when needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Use large blossom pieces appropriate for toddlers.

activities.title: Blossoms in the Breeze
activities.objective: Strengthen gross motor skills while pretending to be blossoms blowing in the wind.
activities.description: Children pretend to be blossoms growing on trees before floating gently to the ground like flower petals.
activities.materials:
Music player
Scarves
Artificial flower petals
activities.setup: Create a large open movement area.
activities.steps:
1. Stand tall like an apple tree.
2. Stretch your branches.
3. Wiggle like blossoms in the breeze.
4. Slowly float to the ground like petals.
5. Stand up and grow into a tree again.
activities.teacherRole: Model gentle movements while reinforcing vocabulary.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe balance, coordination, and participation.
activities.adaptations: Allow seated movements or teacher assistance if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Maintain clear walking paths and remind children to move carefully.

activities.title: Apple Harvest Crew
activities.objective: Encourage cooperative play while pretending to harvest apples.
activities.description: Children become orchard workers by picking apples, filling baskets, and delivering them to the harvest station.
activities.materials:
Farmer hats
Plastic apples
Baskets
Toy wheelbarrow
activities.setup: Place apples throughout the classroom and create a harvest station.
activities.steps:
1. Put on a farmer hat.
2. Walk through the orchard.
3. Pick an apple.
4. Place it into your basket.
5. Deliver the basket to the harvest station.
6. Repeat until every apple has been collected.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage teamwork and model orchard vocabulary throughout the activity.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe teamwork, communication, and imaginative play.
activities.adaptations: Provide lighter baskets or reduce the walking distance if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Remind children to walk while carrying baskets and keep pathways clear.

activities.title: Sort the Harvest
activities.objective: Practice sorting and counting harvested apples.
activities.description: Children sort apples by color and count how many apples were harvested in each basket.
activities.materials:
Red, green, and yellow plastic apples
Three sorting baskets
Number cards
activities.setup: Mix apples together before beginning.
activities.steps:
1. Choose one apple.
2. Identify its color.
3. Place it into the matching basket.
4. Count the apples in each basket.
5. Compare which basket has the most and least apples.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage counting, comparing, and color recognition.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe one-to-one correspondence and counting accuracy.
activities.adaptations: Begin with only two colors if additional support is needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Use only large manipulatives appropriate for toddlers.

activities.title: Farmer's Harvest Basket
activities.objective: Create a harvest basket filled with apples.
activities.description: Children decorate a paper basket and fill it with colorful paper apples to represent a successful harvest.
activities.materials:
Basket template
Red, green, and yellow paper apples
Glue sticks
Crayons
Stickers
activities.setup: Prepare basket templates before the activity.
activities.steps:
1. Color the basket.
2. Cut or glue apples into the basket.
3. Count the apples.
4. Decorate with stickers.
5. Share your finished harvest basket with the class.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage children to talk about how farmers collect apples.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe fine motor control and counting skills.
activities.adaptations: Provide pre-cut apples or larger materials if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Use child-safe scissors only with close supervision.

activities.title: Harvest Dance
activities.objective: Develop coordination while pretending to harvest apples.
activities.description: Children dance around the room pretending to climb ladders, reach for apples, carry baskets, and celebrate a successful harvest.
activities.materials:
Music player
Plastic apples
Baskets
Scarves
activities.setup: Create a large open movement space.
activities.steps:
1. Pretend to climb a ladder.
2. Reach up high to pick apples.
3. Carefully carry your basket.
4. Deliver your harvest.
5. Celebrate with a happy harvest dance.
activities.teacherRole: Lead movements while reviewing orchard vocabulary.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe coordination, participation, and body awareness.
activities.adaptations: Allow seated participation or shorten movement distances when needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Keep movement areas free of obstacles and encourage walking instead of running.

activities.title: Apple Grocery Store
activities.objective: Practice social skills while pretending to shop for apples.
activities.description: Children take turns being grocery shoppers, cashiers, and store workers while buying and selling apples.
activities.materials:
Toy cash register
Toy apples
Grocery baskets
Play money
Shopping bags
activities.setup: Arrange a pretend grocery store with apple displays and a checkout station.
activities.steps:
1. Choose to be a shopper or cashier.
2. Pick apples for your basket.
3. Walk to the checkout.
4. Pretend to pay for the apples.
5. Trade jobs with a friend.
activities.teacherRole: Model polite greetings, turn-taking, and simple conversations.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe sharing, role-playing, and language development.
activities.adaptations: Provide visual communication cards or simplified roles when needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Use child-safe dramatic play materials and encourage walking indoors.

activities.title: Apple's Journey
activities.objective: Sequence the journey of an apple from tree to table.
activities.description: Children place picture cards in order showing how apples travel from the orchard to the grocery store.
activities.materials:
Picture sequencing cards
Apple life cycle poster
Velcro board
activities.setup: Mix the picture cards before beginning.
activities.steps:
1. Look at each picture.
2. Find the farmer.
3. Find the truck.
4. Find the grocery store.
5. Put the pictures in the correct order together.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage children to explain each step in the apple's journey.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe sequencing skills and understanding of community helpers.
activities.adaptations: Reduce the sequence to three cards if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Use large laminated cards appropriate for toddlers.

activities.title: Pack the Apple Boxes
activities.objective: Practice counting while packing apples into shipping boxes.
activities.description: Children count apples into boxes before they are "delivered" to the grocery store.
activities.materials:
Plastic apples
Small boxes
Number cards
activities.setup: Place empty boxes beside baskets of apples.
activities.steps:
1. Choose a number card.
2. Count the correct number of apples.
3. Pack the apples into the box.
4. Count together.
5. Deliver the box to the pretend truck.
activities.teacherRole: Model one-to-one correspondence and encourage counting aloud.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe counting accuracy and confidence.
activities.adaptations: Use smaller numbers or teacher support when needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Use lightweight boxes and large manipulatives.

activities.title: Delivery Driver Adventure
activities.objective: Strengthen gross motor skills while pretending to deliver apples.
activities.description: Children pretend to drive delivery trucks, stop at traffic signs, unload apple boxes, and deliver fresh apples to the grocery store.
activities.materials:
Toy steering wheels
Cones
Apple boxes
Music player
activities.setup: Create a pretend road with cones and delivery stations.
activities.steps:
1. Pretend to drive your truck.
2. Stop at the stop sign.
3. Drive carefully to the grocery store.
4. Unload the apple boxes.
5. Wave goodbye and drive back for another delivery.
activities.teacherRole: Model safe driving, listening skills, and teamwork.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe coordination, listening, and participation.
activities.adaptations: Allow children to walk the route instead of pretending to drive if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Maintain clear pathways and remind children to move safely at all times.

activities.title: Apple Orchard Review
activities.objective: Review the apple growing process and orchard vocabulary.
activities.description: Children use picture cards to retell the story of how apples grow, are harvested, and arrive at grocery stores.
activities.materials:
Apple life cycle cards
Orchard picture cards
Apple tree poster
activities.setup: Lay all picture cards on the floor in random order.
activities.steps:
1. Find the apple tree.
2. Find the blossoms.
3. Find the apples growing.
4. Find the harvest.
5. Find the grocery store.
6. Tell the story together.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage children to explain each step using complete sentences whenever possible.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's understanding of the apple growing process.
activities.adaptations: Reduce the number of sequencing cards if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Use large laminated cards and supervise closely.

activities.title: My Favorite Orchard Memory
activities.objective: Reflect on the week's learning through art.
activities.description: Children create a picture showing their favorite part of Apple Orchard Week, such as picking apples, visiting the orchard, or shopping at the apple market.
activities.materials:
Construction paper
Crayons
Markers
Apple stickers
Glue
Dot markers
activities.setup: Arrange all art materials at the table.
activities.steps:
1. Think about your favorite activity this week.
2. Draw your picture.
3. Decorate with apple stickers.
4. Tell the teacher about your artwork.
5. Display the pictures in the classroom.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage children to describe their artwork and recall the week's learning.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe language development, creativity, and fine motor skills.
activities.adaptations: Provide adaptive crayons, larger paper, or additional support if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Use only non-toxic art supplies.

activities.title: Apple Orchard Relay Count
activities.objective: Practice counting while working together.
activities.description: Children work in teams to collect apples from the orchard and count how many apples each team gathered.
activities.materials:
Plastic apples
Baskets
Number cards
Cones
activities.setup: Scatter apples throughout the activity area.
activities.steps:
1. Walk to the orchard.
2. Pick one apple.
3. Carry it back to your basket.
4. Count the apples together.
5. Repeat until every apple has been collected.
activities.teacherRole: Model counting strategies and encourage teamwork instead of competition.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe counting accuracy, cooperation, and participation.
activities.adaptations: Reduce walking distance or number of apples if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Encourage walking feet and safe carrying of baskets.

activities.title: Apple Orchard Parade
activities.objective: Celebrate everything learned through music, movement, and imaginative play.
activities.description: Children wear farmer hats, carry baskets of pretend apples, march through the classroom, sing apple songs, and celebrate becoming Little Apple Farmers.
activities.materials:
Farmer hats
Plastic apples
Baskets
Music player
Scarves
activities.setup: Create a parade route around the classroom.
activities.steps:
1. Put on your farmer hat.
2. Carry your apple basket.
3. March around the classroom.
4. Sing your favorite apple song.
5. Celebrate with a group cheer and high-fives.
activities.teacherRole: Lead the parade while encouraging children to recall vocabulary and celebrate their accomplishments.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe participation, confidence, coordination, and enthusiasm.
activities.adaptations: Allow seated participation or smaller movements as needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Maintain clear walking paths and encourage safe movement throughout the celebration.

activities.title: Make Homemade Applesauce
activities.objective: Introduce children to preparing a simple healthy snack.
activities.description: Children help mash soft cooked apples into applesauce while observing changes in texture and smell.
activities.materials:
Soft cooked apples
Potato masher
Mixing bowl
Wooden spoons
Cinnamon (optional)
activities.setup: Cook apples before class and allow them to cool to a safe temperature.
activities.steps:
1. Look at the cooked apples.
2. Smell the apples.
3. Mash the apples together.
4. Stir the applesauce.
5. Taste a small spoonful if permitted.
activities.teacherRole: Discuss each cooking step while encouraging descriptive language about texture, smell, and taste.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe willingness to participate, sensory exploration, and communication.
activities.adaptations: Offer pre-made applesauce for children unable to participate in mashing.
activities.safetyNotes: Check food allergies, supervise tasting closely, and ensure food is served at a safe temperature.

activities.title: Chef Hat Decorating
activities.objective: Create a personalized chef hat for dramatic play.
activities.description: Children decorate paper chef hats using apple stickers, crayons, and dot markers before wearing them throughout the week.
activities.materials:
Paper chef hats
Apple stickers
Dot markers
Crayons
Glue
activities.setup: Prepare hats before the activity begins.
activities.steps:
1. Write your name on your hat.
2. Decorate with apples.
3. Color your hat.
4. Add stickers.
5. Wear your chef hat proudly.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage creativity while discussing what chefs do in the kitchen.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe pencil grip, creativity, and participation.
activities.adaptations: Provide larger stickers or adaptive crayons if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Use non-toxic art materials.

activities.title: Measure the Ingredients
activities.objective: Introduce measuring tools used in cooking.
activities.description: Children explore measuring cups and pretend to measure apples, oats, or pom-poms while learning about full and empty.
activities.materials:
Measuring cups
Toy apples
Pom-poms
Bowls
activities.setup: Place measuring cups beside bowls filled with manipulatives.
activities.steps:
1. Scoop ingredients.
2. Fill the measuring cup.
3. Pour into the bowl.
4. Compare full and empty.
5. Repeat with different cups.
activities.teacherRole: Model measuring vocabulary and encourage exploration.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe measuring skills and hand-eye coordination.
activities.adaptations: Provide larger measuring cups or teacher assistance.
activities.safetyNotes: Use only child-safe manipulatives.

activities.title: Little Apple Kitchen
activities.objective: Encourage imaginative play using kitchen tools.
activities.description: Children pretend to prepare apple recipes by washing, stirring, mixing, serving, and sharing pretend apple meals with classmates.
activities.materials:
Play kitchen
Toy apples
Pots
Pans
Mixing bowls
Wooden spoons
Aprons
activities.setup: Arrange a complete pretend kitchen area.
activities.steps:
1. Wash the apples.
2. Slice the pretend apples.
3. Stir your recipe.
4. Serve your meal.
5. Invite a friend to enjoy your apple dish.
activities.teacherRole: Model cooking vocabulary and encourage sharing and teamwork.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe cooperation, communication, and pretend play skills.
activities.adaptations: Provide visual recipe cards or simplified cooking steps.
activities.safetyNotes: Use only child-safe kitchen equipment and remind children to walk while carrying materials.

activities.title: Mash the Apples
activities.objective: Observe how apples change when they are mashed.
activities.description: Children help mash soft cooked apples into applesauce while exploring changes in texture, smell, and appearance.
activities.materials:
Soft cooked apples
Potato masher
Mixing bowls
Wooden spoons
activities.setup: Place cooled cooked apples into large bowls before children arrive.
activities.steps:
1. Look at the cooked apples.
2. Feel how soft they are.
3. Use the masher to mash the apples.
4. Stir the applesauce together.
5. Observe how the apples changed.
activities.teacherRole: Describe each change using rich vocabulary while encouraging predictions and observations.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's curiosity, participation, and descriptive language.
activities.adaptations: Allow children to stir instead of mash if more appropriate.
activities.safetyNotes: Ensure apples are cooled completely and supervise closely during food activities.

activities.title: Before and After Apples
activities.objective: Compare whole apples with applesauce.
activities.description: Children compare apples and applesauce using their senses and discuss what changed.
activities.materials:
Whole apples
Applesauce
Magnifying glasses
Observation trays
activities.setup: Place apples and applesauce side by side on trays.
activities.steps:
1. Look at the apple.
2. Look at the applesauce.
3. Feel each one.
4. Smell each one.
5. Talk about how they are different.
activities.teacherRole: Guide children in comparing textures, smells, and appearances.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe descriptive language and sensory exploration.
activities.adaptations: Use picture cards showing each step for additional support.
activities.safetyNotes: Monitor children closely during tasting and sensory exploration.

activities.title: Applesauce Jar Craft
activities.objective: Create a pretend jar of homemade applesauce.
activities.description: Children decorate a paper applesauce jar using fingerprints, cotton balls, and apple stickers.
activities.materials:
Jar templates
Brown paint
Cotton balls
Apple stickers
Glue
Crayons
activities.setup: Prepare jar templates before the activity.
activities.steps:
1. Color the jar label.
2. Add brown fingerprint "applesauce."
3. Decorate with apple stickers.
4. Write or trace your name.
5. Display the finished jars.
activities.teacherRole: Discuss homemade applesauce while encouraging creativity.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe creativity and hand control.
activities.adaptations: Offer sponge painting or larger materials if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Use washable, non-toxic paint and supervise closely.

activities.title: Stir the Applesauce
activities.objective: Develop coordination through cooking-themed movement.
activities.description: Children pretend to gather apples, stir giant bowls of applesauce, scoop it into jars, and celebrate with a kitchen dance.
activities.materials:
Music player
Wooden spoons
Empty bowls
Scarves
activities.setup: Arrange bowls around the classroom.
activities.steps:
1. Pretend to gather apples.
2. Stir the applesauce.
3. Scoop it into jars.
4. Place jars on the shelf.
5. Dance like happy little chefs.
activities.teacherRole: Lead the movements while reinforcing cooking vocabulary.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe coordination, participation, and ability to follow directions.
activities.adaptations: Allow seated movements or provide teacher assistance when needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Maintain open movement space and encourage walking instead of running.

activities.title: Apple Juice Investigation
activities.objective: Compare apples and apple juice using the senses.
activities.description: Children observe, smell, and taste apple juice while comparing it to whole apples.
activities.materials:
Whole apples
Apple juice
Clear cups
Observation tray
activities.setup: Pour small amounts of apple juice into cups before the activity begins.
activities.steps:
1. Look at the apple.
2. Look at the juice.
3. Smell both.
4. Taste the juice if permitted.
5. Talk about how they are alike and different.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage children to describe color, smell, taste, and texture using new vocabulary.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe descriptive language, curiosity, and willingness to explore new foods.
activities.adaptations: Provide visual vocabulary cards or allow observation without tasting if preferred.
activities.safetyNotes: Check food allergies before tasting and supervise children while drinking.

activities.title: Pour and Measure
activities.objective: Practice measuring and pouring liquids.
activities.description: Children use measuring cups and small pitchers to pour apple juice or colored water between containers while learning full, empty, and half full.

Small pitchers
Measuring cups
Funnels
Colored water or apple juice
Plastic trays

Pitchers

Pretend menus

Rolling pins

activities.title: Apple Pie Dough

Play dough
Rolling pins
Pie pans
Cookie cutters
Plastic apples

1. Roll the dough.

3. Place it into the pie pan.

activities.observationOpportunities: Observe hand strength, coordination, and creativity.

Measuring cups
Measuring spoons
Rice or oats
Bowls
Funnels

activities.observationOpportunities: Observe measuring skills and one-to-one correspondence.
activities.adaptations: Use larger scoops or provide teacher assistance.
activities.safetyNotes: Use only child-safe sensory materials.

activities.title: Bakery Dance Party
activities.objective: Develop gross motor skills while pretending to bake.

Music player
Mixing bowls
Wooden spoons
Scarves

2. Roll the dough.

5. Celebrate with a happy baker dance.
activities.teacherRole: Lead children through each baking motion while reinforcing kitchen vocabulary.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe coordination, participation, and ability to follow directions.
activities.adaptations: Allow seated participation or simplify movements if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Maintain open space and encourage safe movement throughout the activity.

activities.title: Apple Recipe Review

Recipe picture cards
Apple foods
Sequencing cards
Pocket chart

activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's understanding of simple recipes and sequencing.

Drawing paper
Crayons

Glue
Class binder

activities.teacherRole: Write each child's words exactly as spoken and encourage conversation about healthy foods.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe drawing skills, vocabulary, and recall of weekly learning.
activities.adaptations: Provide larger paper, adaptive crayons, or picture choices if needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Use only non-toxic art materials.

activities.title: Kitchen Measuring Relay

Measuring cups
Measuring spoons
Rice or pom-poms
Large bowl
Number cards

activities.title: Little Apple Chef Parade

Mixing bowls

activities.observationOpportunities: Observe participation, coordination, confidence, and enthusiasm.

activities.safetyNotes: Maintain clear walking paths and encourage safe movement throughout the celebration.

activities.title: Apple Seed Discovery

Apples cut in half
Apple seeds
Magnifying glasses
Observation trays

2. Find the seeds.
3. Count the seeds together.
4. Look at the seeds with a magnifying glass.
5. Talk about how seeds grow into trees.
activities.teacherRole: Encourage curiosity and ask open-ended questions about what children notice.

Glue sticks

Apple seeds
Number cards 1–5
Small bowls

2. Count the seeds.
3. Match the seeds to the number.

5. Try another number.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe counting accuracy and attention.
activities.adaptations: Use larger counting objects if necessary.
activities.safetyNotes: Closely supervise all small materials.

activities.observationOpportunities: Observe balance, coordination, and participation.

Apple seeds
Soil
Small cups or pots
Spray bottles
Craft sticks
Markers

1. Fill your cup with soil.
2. Place one apple seed inside.
3. Cover it gently with soil.
4. Spray the soil with water.
5. Write your name on a plant marker.
6. Place your seed near sunlight.
activities.teacherRole: Explain each planting step while discussing what plants need to survive.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe children's understanding of the planting process and their ability to follow directions.
activities.adaptations: Provide larger containers or hand-over-hand assistance when needed.
activities.safetyNotes: Closely supervise soil use and encourage handwashing after planting.

Potting soil
Plastic flowers
Rocks
Toy worms
Gardening tools
Plastic flower pots

activities.steps:
1. Read story aloud.
2. Point to pictures.
3. Name celebration items.
activities.observationOpportunities:
Engagement during New Year Story Time
Use of new year's vocabulary or interest
Cue reading and calm participation
activities.adaptations: Shorten to 1–5 minutes. Offer side-lying or supported positions. Stop immediately if the infant shows overstimulation cues.
activities.safetyNotes: Remain within arm's reach at all times. Use only large, choke-safe materials. Never leave an infant unattended on a mat, changing surface, or near water.

inApp.title: Welcome to Little Learner Hub! 💜
inApp.body:
Thank you so much for joining Little Learner Hub!

I’m so happy you’re here. As a childcare provider myself, I created this platform to save educators time, reduce stress, and make lesson planning easier.

As a Free Member, you can start exploring free lesson plans, activities, and resources right away.

One thing that makes Little Learner Hub different is that it’s constantly growing. I build new features, lesson plans, and tools based on what childcare providers actually need.

Have an idea that would make your day easier? Looking for a specific theme, age group, activity, or feature?

Send me a message anytime through Little Learner Hub.

I personally read every message, and many of the updates you see are inspired by suggestions from providers just like you. I’m building this platform for you, so your feedback truly matters.

Whenever you’re ready, you can upgrade to Pro to unlock the complete curriculum library, premium tools, and every new feature as it’s released.

Thank you again for being here. I can’t wait to keep building Little Learner Hub with you! 💜

inApp.title: Welcome to Your Pro Trial! 🎉
inApp.body:
Thanks for starting your Pro trial!

Over the next 7 days, you’ll get to explore the Pro experience and see how Little Learner Hub can save you time every week.

During your trial you can:

• Browse and explore the complete curriculum library.
• Open and preview every Pro lesson plan.
• Save lesson plans to your calendar.
• Try Pro tools and features.
• Download or print up to 3 premium lesson plans during your trial.

The download limit only applies during the trial. Once you become a Pro member, you’ll have unlimited access to your curriculum library and premium resources.

I’m building Little Learner Hub for childcare providers, so your feedback means everything to me.

Need a lesson plan for a specific theme or age group? Wish a feature worked differently? Have an idea that would make your day easier?

Send me a message anytime inside Little Learner Hub. I personally read every message, and many updates come directly from suggestions from providers like you.

Thank you for giving Little Learner Hub a try. I hope it becomes a tool you love using every day! 💜

inApp.title: Thank You for Becoming a Pro Member! 💜

Your support means more than you know. Every subscription helps me continue building Little Learner Hub into the platform childcare providers deserve.

You now have unlimited access to the full curriculum library, premium lesson plans, activities, planning tools, and every new Pro feature as it’s released.

I’m not building Little Learner Hub for childcare providers—I’m building it with childcare providers.
